problems.title: Release the root-owned sleep inhibitor an interrupted omarchy update left behind
problems.symptom:
Suspend from the system menu silently does nothing, and `systemctl suspend` is refused, hours after an `omarchy update` that was interrupted or killed. Nothing is updating. `systemd-inhibit --list` still shows:

```
WHO             WHAT        WHY                         MODE
omarchy-update  sleep:idle  Omarchy update in progress  block
```

Running `omarchy-update-stay-awake stop` prints `Failed to stop the Omarchy update sleep inhibitor.` It first looks like a laptop or NVIDIA suspend bug.
problems.cause: On Omarchy 4.0.4-1 stable, `/usr/bin/omarchy-update-stay-awake start` launches `sudo systemd-inhibit --what=sleep:idle --who=omarchy-update ... --mode=block sleep infinity &` (or `pkexec` when stdin is not a terminal) and records `$!` in `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/omarchy-update-stay-awake/inhibit-pid`. That PID is the root-owned `sudo` process. `stop` runs as the desktop user and does `kill "$inhibit_pid" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true`, which fails with EPERM and is swallowed. When the update is interrupted before its own cleanup, the privileged inhibitor survives with no owner, and because `start` begins by calling `stop`, later updates cannot clear it either. Confirmed by reading the 4.0.4-1 script on this workstation. Upstream `quattro` already replaced this with a holder that drops to the invoking user (PR #9467, refined in #13361), but that had not reached stable 4.0.4.
problems.fix:
Make sure nothing is actually updating first:

```bash
pgrep -a omarchy-update; pgrep -ax pacman; pgrep -ax yay
systemd-inhibit --list --no-pager | grep omarchy-update
pgrep -af 'who=omarchy-update'
```

If the only hits are the `systemd-inhibit ... sleep infinity` chain, kill it with privilege, then let the helper clear its state file and the stay-awake idle toggle it set:

```bash
sudo pkill -f -- 'who=omarchy-update'
omarchy-update-stay-awake stop
```

A leftover `sleep infinity` reparented to init is harmless once `systemd-inhibit` is gone, because the inhibitor lock belongs to that process. Remove it anyway if you like:

```bash
pgrep -af '^sleep infinity$'
```

A reboot also clears it. The permanent fix is the upstream rewrite of `omarchy-update-stay-awake`, which arrives with an Omarchy release newer than 4.0.4. Check with `pacman -Q omarchy`.
problems.danger: Do not kill the inhibitor while an update is genuinely running. Suspending mid-transaction is exactly what it exists to prevent, and a suspend or power loss during the pacman step can leave packages half-installed.
problems.verify: `systemd-inhibit --list --no-pager | grep omarchy-update` prints nothing, `ls $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/omarchy-update-stay-awake/` reports no such directory or an empty one, and Suspend from the system menu now suspends the machine.

problems.title: Run omarchy update on a non-English locale when it aborts with 'unsafe Omarchy update inhibitor state path'
problems.symptom:
`omarchy update` stops right after the snapshot step and never upgrades anything:

```
Create system snapshot
Snapshots can be selected during boot.
Refusing to use an unsafe Omarchy update inhibitor state path.

Something went wrong during the update!
...
Refusing to use an unsafe Omarchy update inhibitor state path.
```

The desktop language is French, German, Spanish, Portuguese, Hungarian, Chinese or similar. The bar's update icon and the menu entry fail the same way every time.
problems.cause: Builds on the dev and edge channels (`omarchy-dev` 4.0.0.rNNNN, reported from about r2304 to r6694) ship a hardened `omarchy-update-stay-awake`. Its `root_owned_parent_chain()` walks `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` up to `/` and runs `stat -Lc '%u %a %F'`, then requires `$type == "directory"`. coreutils translates `%F`, so it prints `répertoire`, `directorio`, `diretório`, `könyvtár` or `目录`, the comparison always fails, the helper calls `fail_state_boundary`, and `omarchy-update` (under `set -e`) aborts before pacman runs. The stable 4.0.4-1 helper on this workstation has no `%F` check and is not affected. Fixes are open upstream (PR #13352 forces `LC_ALL=C` on that `stat`, #14023 drops the redundant check) but neither was merged as of 2026-10-04.
problems.fix:
Run the update from a terminal with the C locale for that one command. It only changes the language of command output for this run:

```bash
LC_ALL=C omarchy update
```

The bar's update icon and the Omarchy menu cannot take that prefix. Both run `omarchy-launch-floating-terminal-with-presentation omarchy-update`, which starts a non-interactive `bash -c` that reads no rc file, inside the Hyprland session environment, and `/usr/share/omarchy/default/hypr/envs.lua` puts `/usr/share/omarchy/bin` first on that PATH. A PATH shim in `~/.bashrc` or in the uwsm environment never reaches them. Use the terminal until a package carrying PR #13352 or #14023 lands. Check whether the installed helper still has the localized check:

```bash
pacman -Q omarchy-dev omarchy 2>/dev/null
grep -c "%u %a %F" /usr/share/omarchy/bin/omarchy-update-stay-awake   # 0 means fixed
```

Do not patch `/usr/share/omarchy/bin` in place: `omarchy-update-system-pkgs` reinstalls that tree with `--overwrite '/usr/share/omarchy/*'`.
problems.verify: `stat -Lc '%F' /run/user` prints a translated word (confirms you are affected) while `LC_ALL=C omarchy update` runs past `Create system snapshot` into `Update system packages` and finishes without the red banner.
problems.audit_note: The bug and the LC_ALL=C workaround are confirmed: issues #13320, #13385, #13892 and #14087 are open, PR #13352 and #14023 are open and unmerged, the quattro helper still has `/usr/bin/stat -Lc '%u %a %F'` at line 71, and the stable 4.0.4-1 helper here has no such check. The PATH shim is wrong for the stated purpose. The bar widget (shell/plugins/bar/widgets/SystemUpdate.qml) and the menu run omarchy-launch-floating-terminal-with-presentation, which starts `bash -c`, not `bash -lc`, so ~/.bashrc is never read. In addition default/hypr/envs.lua (stable and quattro) moves /usr/share/omarchy/bin to the front of the Hyprland session PATH, so even a session-level PATH entry cannot get ahead of the real helper. The shim therefore never takes effect from the menu. Fix rewritten to drop it.

problems.title: Bring the bar back when omarchy update ends with no shell running
problems.symptom:
`omarchy update` reports success, prints `Restarting shell` and `All plugins have been reloaded`, and then the bar is gone. Super+Space and every menu keybinding do nothing, notifications stop, but Hyprland and windows work. The supervisor logged no `relaunching` or `Giving up` line. The user journal shows a 5 to 6 second gap and then a refusal:

```
omarchy-shell[931]:  INFO: Exiting due to IPC request.
omarchy-shell[3248]: An instance of this configuration is already running.
```

Running `omarchy restart shell` by hand may print `Omarchy shell did not become ready after restart.` and exit 1 even though the bar appears a few seconds later.
problems.cause: `omarchy-update-restart` ends with `omarchy-restart-shell || true`. On 4.0.4-1 that script runs `while timeout 5 quickshell kill -p "$CONFIG_DIR" --any-display; do :; done` and then launches `omarchy-launch-shell`. When the old shell takes more than 5 seconds to tear down, which is common right after an update has replaced its QML, `timeout` ends the wait, the loop exits, and the replacement `quickshell -n` (no-duplicate) sees the dying instance still registered and exits 0. `omarchy-launch-shell` treats exit 0 as a deliberate stop (`(( status == 0 )) && exit 0`), so nothing relaunches, and `|| true` hides the failure from the update. Separately, the restart's readiness poll is 20 attempts at 0.1 s with a 0.5 s IPC timeout, about 2 seconds, while a cold start measured 5 to 6 seconds on slow hardware, hence the false `did not become ready`. Both loops confirmed in the 4.0.4-1 scripts on this workstation. This is a different failure from the crash loop where the supervisor gives up after 6 relaunches.
problems.fix:
From a terminal in your unlocked desktop session:

```bash
omarchy restart shell
```

If it prints `Omarchy shell did not become ready after restart.`, wait about ten seconds before doing anything else, then check rather than re-running it:

```bash
OMARCHY_SHELL_IPC_TIMEOUT=10s omarchy-shell shell ping   # expect: ok
hyprctl layers | grep omarchy-bar
quickshell list -p /usr/share/omarchy/shell | grep -c '^Instance'   # expect: 1
```

Do not use `quickshell list --all` for that count: it also lists Quickshell instances of other configs.

To confirm this was the restart race and not a crash:

```bash
journalctl --user -b -t omarchy-shell --no-pager | grep -E 'Exiting due to IPC|already running|relaunching|Giving up'
```

`Exiting due to IPC request` followed within seconds by `already running`, with no `relaunching` line, is this problem.

Use `omarchy restart shell`, not `omarchy refresh shell`: the refresh resets `~/.config/omarchy/shell.json` to defaults and throws away a customised bar layout.
problems.danger: Never run `omarchy restart shell` over ssh or while the session is locked. On a locked session it re-locks and waits for the lock to come back, and Omarchy 4's lock screen cannot be released headlessly. `omarchy refresh shell` overwrites `~/.config/omarchy/shell.json`.
problems.verify: `omarchy-shell shell ping` prints `ok`, `hyprctl layers` lists the `omarchy-bar` namespace, `quickshell list --all` shows exactly one instance, and Super+Space opens the menu.
problems.audit_note: Read omarchy-restart-shell, omarchy-launch-shell and omarchy-update-restart on 4.0.4-1: the `while timeout 5 quickshell kill ...` loop, the `quickshell -n` launch, `(( status == 0 )) && exit 0`, the 20 x 0.1 s ping loop with a 0.5 s IPC timeout, and `omarchy-restart-shell || true` are all as described. omarchy-refresh-shell does run omarchy-refresh-config omarchy/shell.json, so the warning holds. The hyprctl layers namespace omarchy-bar exists here. One check is wrong: `quickshell list --all` lists every Quickshell config, and on this workstation it returns three instances (one Omarchy, two from /usr/share/flea), so the expected count of 1 fails on a healthy machine. `quickshell list -p /usr/share/omarchy/shell` returned exactly 1. Issues #14085, #14013, #14012 and #13995 are open and on topic. The restart itself was not exercised.

problems.title: Unstick an 'omarchy update -y' that hangs after the orphan list or the kernel update
problems.symptom:
An unattended `omarchy update -y` (from a script, an agent, ssh or a supervisor) stops producing output and never exits. The last lines are an orphan list:

```
Orphan system packages
  asar
  vulkan-headers

<nothing more>
```

or it got further and stops after a kernel or Hyprland upgrade. `/tmp/omarchy-update.log` ends in a box drawing asking `Remove N orphaned package(s)?` or `Linux kernel has been updated. Reboot?`. Keystrokes sent to the process are echoed back rather than answering.
problems.cause: `-y` sets `OMARCHY_UPDATE_UNATTENDED=1`, documented in `omarchy-update` as a promise not to ask anything, but two steps on 4.0.4-1 ignore it. `omarchy-update-orphan-pkgs` decides interactivity only from `[[ ! -t 0 || ! -t 1 ]]`, and `omarchy-update` re-executes itself under `script -qefc ... /tmp/omarchy-update.log`, which supplies a pty, so the guard passes and `gum confirm` waits forever. `omarchy-update-restart`'s `confirm_reboot()` on 4.0.4-1 is a bare `gum confirm "$1"` with no unattended check at all. Both confirmed by reading the scripts on this workstation. By the time either prompt appears the package transaction has already completed, so the system is fine and only the tail of the update (log analysis, status, shell restart) is waiting.
problems.fix:
From another shell, find the waiting `gum` and kill it. Killing it answers no and the update carries on to the next step:

```bash
pgrep -af 'gum confirm'
pkill -f 'gum confirm --default=false Remove'          # the orphan prompt
pkill -f 'gum confirm Linux kernel has been updated'   # reboot prompt after a kernel upgrade
pkill -f 'gum confirm Hyprland has been updated'       # reboot prompt after a Hyprland upgrade
pkill -f 'gum confirm Updates require reboot'          # reboot prompt from the reboot-required marker
```

To avoid the orphan prompt on unattended runs, review and clear orphans beforehand in an interactive terminal:

```bash
pacman -Qtdq
omarchy-update-orphan-pkgs      # asks, then runs sudo pacman -Rns on the list
```

There is no flag that skips the reboot prompts on 4.0.4-1. On `quattro`, `confirm_reboot` already prints `Run omarchy-system-reboot when ready.` instead of asking when `-y` is used, so that half goes away with a later release. Until then, expect to kill one prompt on any run that upgrades the kernel or Hyprland, then reboot when convenient.
problems.danger: Removing orphans with `pacman -Rns` can remove build dependencies or tools you installed as dependencies and still use. Read the list before answering yes.
problems.verify: The update prints its final status and `Restarting shell`, the process exits, and `pgrep -af 'omarchy-update|gum confirm'` returns nothing.
problems.audit_note: Confirmed on 4.0.4-1: omarchy-update-orphan-pkgs guards only on `[[ ! -t 0 || ! -t 1 ]]`, omarchy-update re-execs under `script -qefc`, and confirm_reboot in omarchy-update-restart is a bare `gum confirm "$1"`. The cause holds. The fix is incomplete: omarchy-update-restart has three reboot prompts, `Linux kernel has been updated. Reboot?`, `Updates require reboot. Ready?` and `Hyprland has been updated. Reboot?`, and the record's pkill covers only the first although its symptom names a Hyprland upgrade. Killing gum makes `gum confirm` return non-zero, so the orphan step prints 'Keeping orphaned packages.' and confirm_reboot falls through. Issue #13416 shows quattro's confirm_reboot already checks OMARCHY_UPDATE_UNATTENDED, which supports 'no flag on 4.0.4-1' and points at the fix. Not exercised: no update was run.

problems.title: Fix 'OMARCHY_PATH: unbound variable' when omarchy update runs from zsh, cron or a stripped shell
problems.symptom:
`omarchy update` takes the snapshot, then aborts:

```
/usr/bin/omarchy-update-dev: line 7: OMARCHY_PATH: unbound variable

Something went wrong during the update!
```

It works from the normal terminal but fails from a zsh started as a non-login shell, a cron job or systemd timer, an agent or editor terminal, or `sudo omarchy update`. Related commands fail the same way:

```
/usr/bin/omarchy-channel-current: line 10: OMARCHY_PATH: unbound variable
```
problems.cause: `omarchy-update-dev` and `omarchy-channel-current` run under `set -euo pipefail` and read `$OMARCHY_PATH` with no default (`[[ $OMARCHY_PATH != "/usr/share/omarchy" ]] || exit 0`), confirmed in the 4.0.4-1 scripts here. The variable is only exported by `/usr/share/omarchy/default/bash/env-bootstrap`, which is sourced from `/etc/profile.d/omarchy.sh` (login shells), `~/.bashrc`, the uwsm session env and the bash rc chain. A non-login zsh reads none of those (`/etc/zsh/zprofile` is login-only), cron and `env -i` start empty, and `sudo` resets the environment, so the variable is unset and `set -u` kills the update after the snapshot is already taken.
problems.fix:
Run the update through a bash login shell, as your own user, never through sudo:

```bash
bash -lc 'omarchy update'
```

If zsh is your shell, make every zsh pick up the Omarchy environment by adding this to `~/.zshenv` (read by login and non-login zsh alike):

```sh
[ -r /usr/share/omarchy/default/bash/env-bootstrap ] &&
  . /usr/share/omarchy/default/bash/env-bootstrap
```

For a cron job or systemd user timer, call `bash -lc 'omarchy update -y'` rather than the bare command, or set `OMARCHY_PATH=/usr/share/omarchy` in the unit's `Environment=`.
problems.verify: `zsh -c 'echo $OMARCHY_PATH'` prints `/usr/share/omarchy`, and `omarchy update` gets past `Create system snapshot` without the unbound-variable line.

problems.title: Repair mise tools left root-owned by running 'sudo omarchy update'
problems.symptom:
After running the update under sudo with your environment kept (`sudo -E omarchy update`, or a sudoers `env_keep` that keeps HOME), mise tools stop updating:

```
$ mise use -g opencode
mise ✗ opencode@1.18.32  3ms · failed: Permission denied (os error 13)
mise ERROR Failed to install aqua:anomalyco/opencode@latest: Permission denied (os error 13)
```

The header of `omarchy-update` says `omarchy:requires-sudo=true`, so the sudo looked right. The Omarchy menu under Setup > Defaults > Agent fails with `Could not set <name> as the default coding agent`, while already-installed agents still launch. `find ~ -xdev ! -user "$USER"` lists hundreds of files.
problems.cause: `omarchy-update` escalates only the steps that need root (paccache, snapper, pacman) with its own `sudo` calls. The per-user steps, including `omarchy-update-mise`, which runs `MISE_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE=0 mise up`, are meant to run as the user. When an outer sudo keeps your environment, the whole chain runs as root with your `$HOME`, so mise writes root-owned installs, symlinks and caches under `~/.local/share/mise` and `~/.cache/mise`, and later user-level `mise use -g` cannot replace them. With Arch's default sudo settings a plain `sudo omarchy update` resets HOME to `/root` and drops `OMARCHY_PATH`, so on 4.0.4-1 it aborts earlier at `omarchy-update-dev: line 7: OMARCHY_PATH: unbound variable` and never reaches mise. Confirmed in the 4.0.4-1 `omarchy-update`, `omarchy-update-dev` and `omarchy-update-mise` here.
problems.fix:
Give your files back, then always run the update as yourself:

```bash
find ~ -xdev ! -user "$USER" | head -50     # see what root took
sudo chown -R "$USER:$(id -gn)" ~/.local/share/mise ~/.cache/mise ~/.config/mise
omarchy update                                # no sudo in front
```

If the `find` lists other paths (for example under `~/.cache/yay`), chown those as well. The same rule holds for every `omarchy-*` command: they call sudo themselves where needed. If a plain `sudo omarchy update` stopped with `OMARCHY_PATH: unbound variable` instead, nothing was written to your home and only the last line applies.
problems.danger: Check the `find` output before a recursive chown. Only chown paths inside your own home directory.
problems.verify: `find ~ -xdev ! -user "$USER"` prints nothing, and `mise use -g gh` completes without `Permission denied`.
problems.audit_note: omarchy-update on 4.0.4-1 does carry `omarchy:requires-sudo=true` and escalates only paccache, snapper and pacman. omarchy-update-mise runs `MISE_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE=0 mise up` with no privilege handling. Issue #13329 (open, 4.0.4-1) reports 588 root-owned files after `sudo omarchy update -y`. The cause overstates the trigger. With Arch's default sudo (env_reset), sudo sets HOME to /root and drops OMARCHY_PATH, so a plain `sudo omarchy update` on 4.0.4-1 aborts at `omarchy-update-dev: line 7: OMARCHY_PATH: unbound variable` before the mise step (issue #12858), and even if it got that far mise would write under /root. Your own home gets root-owned files only when sudo keeps HOME and OMARCHY_PATH, as `sudo -E` or a sudoers env_keep does. I could not read /etc/sudoers here to see whether Omarchy changes this, so medium confidence. The chown fix is correct. The group is now taken from `id -gn` rather than assumed.

problems.title: Finish an update that a migration aborted with 'could not put ... on the bar: omarchy-shell is not responding'
problems.symptom:
`omarchy update` aborts during migrations, after the package step succeeded:

```
Running migration (1789581661)
Install Elsewhen, the world clock plugin
...
omarchy-bar: could not put omacom.elsewhen on the bar: omarchy-shell is not responding

Something went wrong during the update!
```

Re-running fails at the same migration, sometimes several times in a row. Migration `1790042972` fails the same way. Often seen when switching from stable to edge.
problems.cause: `omarchy-shell` wraps every IPC call in `timeout ${OMARCHY_SHELL_IPC_TIMEOUT:-2s}` and maps a timeout to `omarchy-shell is not responding`. `ask_to_put` in `omarchy-bar` retries 50 times when the shell is starting (`not ready`) or absent, but treats a timeout as fatal on the first attempt. During an update the shell is busy reloading the QML the same transaction just replaced, and the migration calls `rescanPlugins` on the line before the put, so the put often outlasts 2 seconds even though the shell does write the widget into `shell.json`. The migration dies under `set -euo pipefail`, `omarchy-migrate` writes no completion marker, and every later step (hooks, AUR, mise, orphans, shell restart) is skipped. Reported on `omarchy-dev` r2186 and r2304. Neither migration is in the stable 4.0.4-1 tree here.
problems.fix:
Give the shell IPC more time for this run. The variable is inherited through `script` and `omarchy-migrate` down to `omarchy-shell`:

```bash
OMARCHY_SHELL_IPC_TIMEOUT=15s omarchy update
```

Alternatively restart the shell first from your unlocked session, give it a few seconds to settle, then retry:

```bash
omarchy restart shell
sleep 10
omarchy update
```

The migrations are idempotent, so a retry finishes them. Check that nothing is left pending:

```bash
ls ~/.local/state/omarchy/migrations/ | sort | tail -3
ls /usr/share/omarchy/migrations/ | sort | tail -3
```
problems.danger: Do not run `omarchy restart shell` over ssh or on a locked session: it re-locks the session and the Omarchy 4 lock screen cannot be released headlessly.
problems.verify: The update ends without the red banner and prints `omacom.elsewhen is on the bar` (or the relevant widget), and the newest migration file name in `/usr/share/omarchy/migrations/` also exists in `~/.local/state/omarchy/migrations/`.

problems.title: Clear a read-only Go module cache that makes an AUR rebuild fail omarchy update
problems.symptom:
The system upgrade and migrations finish, then `Update AUR packages` fails on a Go-based package you installed from the AUR, with thousands of lines like:

```
==> Removing existing $srcdir/ directory...
rm: cannot remove '/home/user/.cache/yay/hyprmoncfg/src/go-mod/github.com/!make!now!just/heredoc@v1.0.0/LICENSE': Permission denied
==> ERROR: An unknown error has occurred. Exiting...
 -> Failed to install the following packages. Manual intervention is required:
hyprmoncfg - signal: user defined signal 1
```

On the edge and dev channels the update then ends with `Something went wrong during the update!` and `'/usr/bin/setpriv' terminated by signal TERM.`. On stable 4.0.4-1 the update carries on past the error, and the AUR package simply stays at its old version on every update.
problems.cause: Some PKGBUILDs set `GOMODCACHE="${srcdir}/go-mod"`. Go creates module-cache directories read-only (`dr-xr-xr-x`), so the previous build leaves `src/go-mod/` behind, and `yay --cleanafter` (which `omarchy-update-aur-pkgs` passes) does not remove it. On the next version bump makepkg cannot delete the old `$srcdir`. On the edge and dev channels `omarchy-update-aur-pkgs` runs `yay ... -Sua ... || exit 1`, so one user-installed AUR package turns the whole update red even though system packages are already upgraded, and the `setpriv terminated by signal TERM` line is the cleanup stopping the stay-awake holder, not a crash. On stable 4.0.4-1 the script has no `|| exit 1` and ends in `echo`, so the update reports success while the package silently stays behind. The proper fix is `-modcacherw` in the PKGBUILD.
problems.fix:
Make the stale tree writable, delete it, and rerun:

```bash
pkg=hyprmoncfg            # the package named in the error
chmod -R u+w ~/.cache/yay/$pkg/src
rm -rf ~/.cache/yay/$pkg/src
omarchy update
```

If several Go packages are affected:

```bash
find ~/.cache/yay -type d -name go-mod -prune -exec chmod -R u+w {} +
```

Ask the package maintainer to add `-modcacherw` to the `go build` and `go test` flags, or to `chmod -R u+w "$srcdir/go-mod"` in `prepare()`, so it does not recur.
problems.verify: `omarchy update` reaches and passes `Update AUR packages`, and `pacman -Q hyprmoncfg` (or the affected package) shows the new version.
problems.audit_note: The makepkg failure and the chmod and rm fix are right and match issue #13334. Two claims in the cause hold only on the edge and dev channels. Stable 4.0.4-1 `/usr/bin/omarchy-update-aur-pkgs` runs `yay -Sua --noconfirm --cleanafter --ignore gcc14,gcc14-libs` with no `|| exit 1` and ends in `echo`, so a failed AUR build prints yay's error and the update carries on to mise, orphans and the shell restart without the red failure banner. The `|| exit 1` is on quattro. The `/usr/bin/setpriv` line comes from quattro's stay-awake holder, which drops to the invoking user with setpriv. The 4.0.4-1 helper has no setpriv. Cause and symptom rewritten to separate the two channels. The fix is unchanged.

problems.title: Stop booting the stock Arch kernel that sits beside linux-omarchy
problems.symptom: `uname -r` shows a stock kernel such as `7.2.3-arch1-3` instead of `7.2.5-3-omarchy`, days or weeks after the update that installed `linux-omarchy` and asked for a reboot. Nothing looks wrong: the migration is marked done and the Limine menu lists `linux-omarchy` first. With Direct Boot enabled, `efibootmgr` shows the Omarchy entry pointing at `\EFI\LINUX\OMARCHY_LINUX.EFI`. Fixes that shipped only in linux-omarchy never take effect, and one report traced btrfs corruption to an accidental boot of the stale stock kernel.
problems.cause: Two kernels are installed on most Omarchy 4 systems. Fresh 4.0.4 ISO installs get stock `linux` from archinstall's base package set, and migration `1789325478` installs `linux-omarchy` but deliberately leaves `linux` installed as a fallback (it only sets `BOOT_ORDER="linux-omarchy, linux-omarchy-*, *, *fallback, Snapshots"` in `/etc/default/limine`). `limine-mkinitcpio` builds one UKI per kernel package, named `omarchy_<pkgname>.efi`, so `omarchy_linux.efi` is the stock kernel and `omarchy_linux-omarchy.efi` is the Omarchy one. Three things then pick the stock one: the shipped template `/usr/share/omarchy/default/limine/limine.conf` hardcodes `default_entry: 2`, an index into a list whose length depends on how many kernels exist (reported to land on stock `linux` on upgraded machines), a Direct Boot EFI entry created before the migration still points at `omarchy_linux.efi` because Direct Boot bypasses Limine and its `BOOT_ORDER`, and `omarchy-setup-direct-boot` picks the UKI with `find ... -name "omarchy*.efi" | head -1`, which is unpredictable with two files. Confirmed on this workstation: `linux 7.2.3.arch1-3` and `linux-omarchy 7.2.5-3` both installed, the template carries `default_entry: 2`, and the UKI name is built as `${UKI_PREFIX}_${KERNEL_NAME}.efi` in `/usr/share/libalpm/scripts/limine-mkinitcpio-install`.
problems.fix:
Check what you are running and what is installed:

```bash
uname -r
pacman -Q linux linux-omarchy
sudo efibootmgr | grep -i omarchy
```

If you are on the stock kernel, reboot and pick `linux-omarchy` by hand in the Omarchy Bootloader menu (Direct Boot users: choose Limine from the firmware boot menu). Use it for a while. Once you are satisfied it works on your hardware, remove the stock kernel while running linux-omarchy. The package's ALPM hooks remove its Limine entry and UKI:

```bash
uname -r | grep -q -- '-omarchy$' && sudo pacman -R linux
```

If pacman refuses because something depends on `linux` (for example a prebuilt `nvidia-open` module package), stop and switch that package to its DKMS or linux-omarchy equivalent first.

With Direct Boot, re-point the EFI entry at the remaining UKI. The script removes the entry on the first run and creates a new one on the second:

```bash
omarchy-setup-direct-boot   # answer yes to: Disable direct boot
omarchy-setup-direct-boot   # answer yes to: Setup direct boot
sudo efibootmgr | grep -i omarchy   # expect ...OMARCHY_LINUX-OMARCHY.EFI
```

Plain Arch with no Omarchy kernel is not affected. Apple T2 Macs keep `linux-t2` and are skipped by the migration on purpose.
problems.danger: Removing `linux` removes your fallback kernel. Several linux-omarchy 7.2.5 regressions were reported on specific hardware (some MacBooks, Wi-Fi chips, PoE devices) where the stock kernel worked, so boot linux-omarchy successfully on your machine before removing the stock one, and keep the Limine snapshot menu available. Never remove the kernel you are currently running.
problems.verify: After a reboot without touching the menu, `uname -r` ends in `-omarchy`, `pacman -Q linux` reports it is not installed, and on Direct Boot systems `sudo efibootmgr -v | grep -i omarchy` names `OMARCHY_LINUX-OMARCHY.EFI`.

problems.title: Boot past 'PANIC: efi: LoadImage failure' by switching Limine from UKI to a plain Linux entry
problems.symptom:
The Omarchy Bootloader menu appears, and choosing the kernel (or letting it time out) halts the machine:

```
PANIC: efi: LoadImage failure (0x8000000000000002)
Stacktrace: <panic+...> <chainload+...> <boot+...> <_menu+...>
End of trace. System halted.
```

`0x8000000000000002` (EFI_INVALID_PARAMETER) is reported on older UEFI laptops such as a Bay Trail ThinkPad Yoga 11e on a fresh install. `0x800000000000000f` (EFI_ACCESS_DENIED) is reported on MSI boards once Secure Boot is turned on for Windows dual-boot, even with the UKI and Limine signed by sbctl. On the old laptop the ISO itself may also fail with `grub_arch_efi_linux_boot_image:227: cannot load image`.
problems.cause: Omarchy 4 boots the kernel as a unified kernel image. `omarchy-settings` ships `/etc/limine-entry-tool.d/omarchy-uki.conf` with `ENABLE_UKI=yes`, overriding `limine-entry-tool`'s own default of `no` in `/etc/limine-entry-tool.conf`, so the Limine entry is `protocol: efi` and Limine hands the UKI to the firmware's `LoadImage()`. Some firmware implements that call badly: old UEFI rejects the image, and MSI firmware affected by sbctl's FQ0001 quirk denies non-factory-signed images. Limine's `protocol: linux` path loads `vmlinuz` and the initramfs itself and never calls `LoadImage()`. `/etc/default/limine` is read last by `limine-common-functions` ("Load /etc/default/limine (highest priority)"), so an `ENABLE_UKI=no` there beats the package drop-in and survives updates. That workaround is confirmed by the MSI reporter in issue #12045. For the old-UEFI case in issue #12143 it follows from the same mechanism but no reporter has confirmed it.
problems.fix:
If the system still boots from another entry, or after you get in:

```bash
echo 'ENABLE_UKI=no' | sudo tee -a /etc/default/limine
sudo limine-mkinitcpio
```

If it does not boot at all, use the Omarchy ISO as a rescue system (on very old firmware, write it with Ventoy and use its GRUB2 mode). Identify partitions with `lsblk -f` and adjust device names below.

Encrypted install (the default):

```bash
cryptsetup open /dev/nvme0n1p2 root
mount -o subvol=@ /dev/mapper/root /mnt
mount -o subvol=@log /dev/mapper/root /mnt/var/log
mount -o subvol=@pkg /dev/mapper/root /mnt/var/cache/pacman/pkg
```

Unencrypted install:

```bash
mount -o subvol=@ /dev/nvme0n1p2 /mnt
mount -o subvol=@log /dev/nvme0n1p2 /mnt/var/log
mount -o subvol=@pkg /dev/nvme0n1p2 /mnt/var/cache/pacman/pkg
```

Then, in both cases:

```bash
mount /dev/nvme0n1p1 /mnt/boot              # the vfat ESP
arch-chroot /mnt
echo 'ENABLE_UKI=no' >> /etc/default/limine
limine-mkinitcpio
exit
```

Edit `/etc/default/limine`, not `omarchy-uki.conf`: the latter is owned by `omarchy-settings` and package updates manage it. Snapshot entries created before the change still point at UKIs and will panic the same way if selected. Snapshots taken afterwards use the new format.
problems.danger: With Secure Boot on, `ENABLE_UKI=no` means the firmware no longer verifies the kernel and initramfs, because Limine loads them itself. Secure Boot then protects only Limine and its enrolled config. Accept that only if Secure Boot is on for Windows rather than for Linux. The rescue steps write to the installed system from a chroot, so check every device name against `lsblk -f` first.
problems.verify: `sudo grep -n 'protocol' /boot/limine.conf` shows `protocol: linux` for the kernel entry, the machine boots through Limine without the panic, and `uname -r` matches the installed kernel.
problems.audit_note: Confirmed here: /etc/limine-entry-tool.d/omarchy-uki.conf (owned by omarchy-settings 4.0.4-1) holds ENABLE_UKI=yes, /etc/limine-entry-tool.conf ships ENABLE_UKI=no, and /usr/lib/limine/limine-common-functions loads /etc/default/limine last as 'highest priority'. Issue #12045 (MSI, Secure Boot) reports ENABLE_UKI=no as a working workaround. Issue #12143 (Bay Trail) has no comments and no confirmed fix, only the Ventoy GRUB2 mode for the ISO, so the cause now marks the old-UEFI case as untested. The rescue block mounted /dev/mapper/root unconditionally, which fails on an unencrypted install, so it now has both branches. Turning off the UKI under Secure Boot means the firmware no longer verifies the kernel and initramfs, which needs a danger. Not exercised: no bootloader change was made.

problems.title: Stop a twitching mouse cancelling the Limine autoboot countdown
problems.symptom: On every power-on the Omarchy Bootloader menu stays up forever instead of booting after the countdown. A pointer drifts across the entries, the countdown stops, and sometimes a different entry ends up highlighted. It only happens on desktops with a USB mouse plugged in, and pressing Enter on the right entry boots normally.
problems.cause: Limine added mouse support in 12.5.0 and it is on by default. Its CONFIG.md says using the mouse stops the `timeout` countdown just as pressing a key does, and optical mice often report motion during POST. Omarchy's shipped template `/usr/share/omarchy/default/limine/limine.conf` has no `mouse:` line (checked on 4.0.4-1, with limine 12.8.0-1 installed).
problems.fix:
Add one global option near the top of `/boot/limine.conf`, above the first line starting with `/`:

```bash
sudo sed -i '0,/^interface_branding:/s//mouse: no\n&/' /boot/limine.conf
sudo grep -n '^mouse\|^timeout\|^default_entry' /boot/limine.conf
```

Or open it with `sudo nano /boot/limine.conf` and add:

```
mouse: no
```

The keyboard still selects snapshots. `limine-entry-tool` rewrites the entries and keeps the global header, but `omarchy-refresh-limine` copies the template over the whole file, so re-add the line after running it.
problems.danger: A typo in the global section of `/boot/limine.conf` can stop the menu from parsing. Keep a copy first: `sudo cp /boot/limine.conf /boot/limine.conf.bak`.
problems.verify: Power on with the mouse connected and moving: the countdown keeps running and the default entry boots on its own.

problems.title: New snapshots missing from the Limine menu for hours after booting from Windows
problems.symptom: On a Windows dual-boot machine, `snapper -c root list` shows the snapshot `omarchy update` just took, the journal says `Saved: snapshots.json` and `Updated: limine.conf`, but the Snapshots submenu in the Omarchy Bootloader has no entry for it or any snapshot after it. The entries appear on their own a few hours later, roughly your UTC offset.
problems.cause: Windows keeps the hardware clock in local time and Linux reads it as UTC. In a time zone east of UTC (a positive offset, such as most of Europe, Africa and Asia), Omarchy therefore starts after a Windows session with the clock ahead by the UTC offset until NTP corrects it. A snapshot taken in that window, such as the pre-update snapshot, carries a future timestamp. limine-snapper-sync (1.31.0 here) records the newest snapshot time as `lastUTCTime` and treats a later snapshot as new only if its time is later than that stamp, so every real-time snapshot afterwards is ignored until real time passes the bad stamp. The tool logs nothing about it. West of UTC the clock runs behind instead, the stray snapshot lies in the past and nothing is hidden. Reported upstream as limine-snapper-sync work item 17.
problems.fix:
Settle on one clock convention so the clock is never wrong at boot. Preferred: make Windows keep UTC. In an elevated Windows command prompt:

```
reg add "HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\TimeZoneInformation" /v RealTimeIsUniversal /d 1 /t REG_DWORD /f
```

Or make Linux read the RTC as local time instead:

```bash
timedatectl set-local-rtc 1
```

Until then, after coming back from Windows, wait for NTP before updating:

```bash
timedatectl show -p NTPSynchronized --value   # wait for: yes
omarchy update
```

Snapshots already hidden reappear once real time passes the future stamp. They are intact in `snapper -c root list` in the meantime.
problems.verify: `timedatectl` shows the correct local time immediately after booting from Windows, and a fresh `omarchy-snapshot create` appears in the Limine Snapshots submenu on the next boot.
problems.audit_note: limine-snapper-sync 1.31.0-1.1 is installed and its binary contains lastUTCTime and setLastUTCTime. GitLab work item 17 resolves and describes exactly this rule, and Omarchy issue #13367 (open, 4.0.4) matches. The registry command and the preference for Windows keeping UTC match the Arch wiki System time page word for word. One gap in the cause: a clock read in local time as UTC runs ahead only in time zones east of UTC. West of UTC it runs behind, the stray snapshot is in the past and nothing is hidden. Cause rewritten to say so. Fix unchanged.

problems.title: Protect Windows and other Linux boot entries before running an Omarchy factory reset
problems.symptom: After `omarchy-system-factory-reset` on a machine that shares its ESP with Windows or another Linux, the Omarchy Bootloader menu lists only Omarchy. Windows still boots from the firmware boot menu, but its Limine entry is gone. A second Linux install managed by limine-entry-tool loses its entry and its `/<machine-id>/` boot directory on the ESP.
problems.cause: `reset_limine_config` in `omarchy-system-factory-reset` (present on 4.0.4-1 here) copies the shipped template over the ESP's `limine.conf`, which removes every entry that is not the new Omarchy one, including `/Windows`. It then deletes the ESP directory of every `machine-id=` the old `limine.conf` referenced except the new one, which includes another limine-entry-tool-managed Linux. The comment in the script says only ids from the old file are removed, but a foreign install's id is in that file too. `omarchy-provision-owner` repeats the same logic on the first boot after the reset (`limine_entries_stale` treats any other machine-id as stale), so a fix applied between the two is lost again. Windows' own boot files under `EFI/Microsoft` survive.
problems.fix:
Before resetting, copy the menu and any foreign boot directories off to the ESP or another disk. The reset swaps the root subvolume, so do not keep the backup in `/root`:

```bash
sudo cp /boot/limine.conf /boot/limine.conf.pre-reset
sudo grep -o 'machine-id=[0-9a-f]\{32\}' /boot/limine.conf | sort -u
cat /etc/machine-id    # this install's id, the only one the reset should replace
```

For any other id printed, copy `/boot/<that-id>/` to a USB drive.

After the reset and after first-boot setup has finished, add Windows back to the end of `/boot/limine.conf`:

```
/Windows
    protocol: efi
    path: boot():/EFI/Microsoft/Boot/bootmgfw.efi
```

Compare with the stanza in `/boot/limine.conf.pre-reset` and copy it exactly if it differs. For another Linux, boot it from the firmware boot menu and rebuild its own entry from inside it (on a limine-entry-tool distro, `sudo limine-mkinitcpio`), or restore its `/boot/<id>/` directory from the backup.
problems.danger: A factory reset discards the user, user-installed packages and `/etc` changes by design. Editing `/boot/limine.conf` wrongly can leave the menu unparseable, so keep the `.pre-reset` copy until every OS boots.
problems.verify: The Omarchy Bootloader menu lists Windows (and the other Linux) again after a reboot, and each one boots from it.

problems.title: Keep your snapshot history when the Quattro upgrade replaces the Snapper config
problems.symptom: A few minutes after upgrading from Omarchy 3 to 4 with `omarchy-upgrade-to-quattro`, nearly all btrfs snapshots are gone, including manual ones and the pre-upgrade snapshot the upgrade itself took. Right after the upgrade everything was still listed. `/etc/snapper/configs/root` now has only a handful of keys, and `/home` snapshots stopped being made.
problems.cause: `configure_snapper_policy()` in the Quattro upgrade runs `install/config/snapper.sh`, which does `install -m 0644 "$template" /etc/snapper/configs/root` with no merge, no backup and no message beyond `Configuring Omarchy Snapper snapshot retention`. The template, `/usr/share/omarchy/default/snapper/root` (checked on 4.0.4-1), sets `NUMBER_LIMIT="5"`, `NUMBER_LIMIT_IMPORTANT="5"`, `NUMBER_MIN_AGE="0"` and `TIMELINE_CREATE="no"`. With a minimum age of 0 the next `snapper-cleanup.timer` run (`OnBootSec=10m`, then hourly) can delete any number-cleanup snapshot beyond the newest 5, however young. The same script also rewrites `/etc/conf.d/snapper` to `SNAPPER_CONFIGS="root"`, de-registering a `home` config. btrfs snapshot deletion is irreversible.
problems.fix:
Stopping `snapper-cleanup.timer` beforehand does not help: the upgrade's own `install/config/snapper.sh` ends with `systemctl enable --now snapper-cleanup.timer`. Protect snapshots in a way the upgrade cannot undo. Snapper's cleanup only deletes snapshots that carry a cleanup algorithm, so a snapshot made without `-c` survives any `NUMBER_LIMIT`.

Before running the Quattro upgrade, save your policy and take a rollback snapshot that cleanup will never touch:

```bash
sudo cp -a /etc/snapper/configs/root /etc/snapper/configs/root.pre-quattro
sudo cp -a /etc/conf.d/snapper /etc/conf.d/snapper.pre-quattro
sudo snapper -c root create -d "before quattro upgrade"
sudo snapper -c root list    # the new snapshot shows an empty Cleanup column
```

For existing snapshots you want to keep, clear their cleanup algorithm the same way, using the numbers from `snapper list`, and check the Cleanup column is empty afterwards:

```bash
sudo snapper -c root modify -c "" 42
```

Right after the upgrade finishes, put back the values you want with snapper itself:

```bash
diff /etc/snapper/configs/root.pre-quattro /etc/snapper/configs/root
sudo snapper -c root set-config NUMBER_MIN_AGE=1800 NUMBER_LIMIT=10 NUMBER_LIMIT_IMPORTANT=10
sudo snapper -c root get-config | grep -E 'NUMBER_|TIMELINE'
```

If you had a `home` config, restore its registration with `sudo cp /etc/conf.d/snapper.pre-quattro /etc/conf.d/snapper` and check `sudo snapper -c home list`.

If the upgrade already ran, do the `set-config` step immediately to protect what is left. Snapshots already deleted cannot be recovered. Snapshots made without a cleanup algorithm are never removed automatically, so delete them yourself with `sudo snapper -c root delete <number>` once you no longer need them.
problems.danger: Raising `NUMBER_LIMIT` keeps more snapshots and more disk space. `omarchy update` refuses to start with under 10 GiB free, so choose limits your root filesystem can hold.
problems.verify: `sudo snapper -c root get-config` shows your `NUMBER_MIN_AGE` and `NUMBER_LIMIT`, and `snapper -c root list` still shows the pre-upgrade snapshot an hour after the upgrade (after at least one `snapper-cleanup.service` run in `journalctl -u snapper-cleanup`).
problems.audit_note: The cause holds: /usr/share/omarchy/install/config/snapper.sh runs `install -m 0644 "$template" /etc/snapper/configs/root`, rewrites /etc/conf.d/snapper to SNAPPER_CONFIGS="root", and the template has NUMBER_MIN_AGE="0", NUMBER_LIMIT="5", NUMBER_LIMIT_IMPORTANT="5", TIMELINE_CREATE="no". The rc branch's omarchy-upgrade-to-quattro calls configure_snapper_policy. Issue #12551 reports 53 snapshots deleted five minutes after the upgrade. The fix's main protection does not work: the same snapper.sh ends with `systemctl enable --now snapper-cleanup.timer limine-snapper-sync.service`, so stopping the timer before the upgrade is undone by the upgrade itself. The fix now protects snapshots in a way snapper.sh cannot reverse. Snapper's cleanup algorithms act only on snapshots that carry a cleanup algorithm, so a snapshot created without -c is never deleted by cleanup. Not exercised: no snapper command was run here.

problems.title: Remove the resume parameters 'omarchy hibernation remove' leaves in the kernel command line
problems.symptom: After `omarchy hibernation remove`, `cat /proc/cmdline` still carries `resume=/dev/mapper/root resume_offset=1929151` pointing at a swapfile that no longer exists. Worse, after setting hibernation up again later, hibernate writes an image and powers off but the next boot starts fresh and the session is lost.
problems.cause: `omarchy-hibernation-setup` writes `/etc/limine-entry-tool.d/resume.conf` (`KERNEL_CMDLINE[default]+=" resume=... resume_offset=..."`). `omarchy-hibernation-remove` on 4.0.4-1 deletes the swapfile, the `/swap` subvolume, the fstab line and `/etc/mkinitcpio.conf.d/omarchy_resume.conf`, then runs `limine-mkinitcpio`, but never deletes `resume.conf`, so the UKI keeps the old parameters. A later setup only writes `resume.conf` when it is missing (`if [[ ! -f $RESUME_DROP_IN ]]`), so the new swapfile's physical offset is never recorded and resume reads the wrong place. Both confirmed by reading the 4.0.4-1 scripts here.
problems.fix:
After removing hibernation, delete the drop-in and rebuild the UKI:

```bash
sudo rm -f /etc/limine-entry-tool.d/resume.conf
sudo limine-mkinitcpio
```

If you are setting hibernation up again and the drop-in survived from an earlier setup, remove it first so setup writes the current offset:

```bash
sudo rm -f /etc/limine-entry-tool.d/resume.conf
omarchy hibernation setup
cat /etc/limine-entry-tool.d/resume.conf
sudo btrfs inspect-internal map-swapfile -r /swap/swapfile   # must equal resume_offset
```
problems.verify: After a reboot, `grep -o 'resume[^ ]*' /proc/cmdline` prints nothing when hibernation is removed, or a `resume_offset` equal to `sudo btrfs inspect-internal map-swapfile -r /swap/swapfile` when it is set up. A test `systemctl hibernate` restores the session.

problems.title: Collect a debug log when 'omarchy debug' says Unknown Omarchy command
problems.symptom:
In a terminal opened from the desktop, `omarchy --help` lists `omarchy debug` under Common commands, and the bug-report instructions say to attach its output, but it fails:

```
$ omarchy debug
Unknown Omarchy command: omarchy debug
Run 'omarchy commands --all' to discover available commands.
```

`omarchy commands --all | grep debug` shows nothing. The same command can work over ssh or on a TTY.
problems.cause: The `omarchy` router only scans the directory it was started from (`OMARCHY_BIN_DIR` is derived from `BASH_SOURCE`) for `omarchy-*` scripts. On 4.0.4-1, `omarchy-debug` is shipped by `omarchy-settings` as a real file at `/usr/bin/omarchy-debug` and is absent from `/usr/share/omarchy/bin`, while the help text hardcodes the route. `/usr/share/omarchy/default/hypr/envs.lua` puts `/usr/share/omarchy/bin` first on the Hyprland session PATH, so every terminal opened from the desktop runs `/usr/share/omarchy/bin/omarchy`, which cannot see it. An ssh or TTY login runs `/usr/bin/omarchy`, which scans `/usr/bin` and does find it. Confirmed on this workstation with `pacman -Qo /usr/bin/omarchy-debug` and by comparing `commands --all` from both routers. The bundled agent skill documentation repeats the broken form.
problems.fix:
Call the script directly. It is on PATH:

```bash
omarchy-debug --no-sudo --print > ~/omarchy-debug.txt
less ~/omarchy-debug.txt
```

Without `--print` it writes the log and offers to upload it. Without `--no-sudo` it asks for your password to include privileged sections.
problems.danger: The debug log includes network details such as MAC and IP addresses of your LAN. Read it before uploading or pasting it into a public issue.
problems.verify: `omarchy-debug --no-sudo --print | head` prints system information instead of `Unknown Omarchy command`.
problems.audit_note: Confirmed: /usr/bin/omarchy-debug is owned by omarchy-settings 4.0.4-1 and /usr/share/omarchy/bin/omarchy-debug does not exist. The router scans its own directory (OMARCHY_BIN_DIR from BASH_SOURCE), and line 532 hardcodes `omarchy debug` in help. The failure depends on which `omarchy` runs, which the cause misses. On this install /usr/bin/omarchy is a regular file, and `/usr/bin/omarchy commands --all` lists `omarchy debug [--no-sudo] [--print]`, while `/usr/share/omarchy/bin/omarchy commands --all` lists nothing. /usr/share/omarchy/default/hypr/envs.lua puts /usr/share/omarchy/bin first on the Hyprland session PATH, so terminals opened from the desktop get the failing router, while ssh and TTY logins resolve /usr/bin/omarchy and the command works. omarchy-debug's usage line confirms `[--no-sudo] [--print]`. Issues #14014 and #13702 are open and match.

problems.title: Stop gh, claude and other mise wrappers printing 'mise ... tools:' before their output
problems.symptom:
Every run of `gh`, `claude`, `codex`, `opencode` and similar tools prints an extra first line:

```
$ gh --version 2>/dev/null
mise ~/.config/mise/config.toml tools: gh@2.102.0
gh version 2.102.0 (2026-09-30)
```

Scripts that capture output break: `gh ... --json` no longer parses, `$(claude --version)` holds two lines, and one user published the status line into a pull request description through `gh pr edit --body-file`.
problems.cause: Omarchy installs these tools as lazy wrappers in `~/.local/bin`, written by `omarchy-mise-install`. Wrappers written before the template gained `--quiet` (installs from about 4.0.1 and earlier) run `mise use -g "<pkg>" || exit 1` on every invocation, and mise prints its status line to stdout. The current template writes `mise use -g --quiet`, but an existing wrapper is only rewritten when a migration happens to regenerate it. The migration that fixes this (`1787573629.sh`) exists on `quattro` but had not reached stable 4.0.4. This workstation still carries 13 such wrappers.
problems.fix:
Regenerate every old-form wrapper through the current template, keeping each wrapper's package and binary:

```bash
for w in ~/.local/bin/*; do
  [[ -f $w && -x $w && ! -L $w ]] || continue
  pkg=$(sed -n 's/^mise use -g "\(.*\)" || exit 1$/\1/p' "$w")
  [[ -n $pkg ]] || continue
  bin=$(sed -n 's/^exec mise x ".*" -- "\([^"]*\)" "\$@"$/\1/p' "$w")
  echo "regenerating $(basename "$w") ($pkg)"
  omarchy-mise-install "$pkg" "$(basename "$w")" "${bin:-$(basename "$w")}"
done
```

The `sed` only matches the old unquiet form, so wrappers already using `--quiet` and real binaries in `~/.local/bin` are left alone.
problems.verify: `grep -L -- '--quiet' $(grep -l 'mise use -g' ~/.local/bin/*)` prints nothing, and `gh --version 2>/dev/null | head -1` starts with `gh version`.

problems.title: Stop an Omarchy mise wrapper (claude, gh, codex, omp) looping forever and burning CPU
problems.symptom: Fans spin up and a core sits busy for hours. `ps` shows a `~/.local/bin/<tool>` process repeatedly running `mise use -g --quiet <tool>` about twice a second in the same PID, often reparented to `systemd --user`. Or the machine becomes progressively unresponsive with thousands of short-lived processes when a terminal or editor calls `omp` or another wrapped tool. GUI apps that probe CLIs with a timeout (Hermes Desktop, Electron tools) report the tool as `Not installed` or hang. Nothing logs an error.
problems.cause: The wrapper `omarchy-mise-install` writes ends with `exec mise x "<pkg>" -- "<bin>" "$@"`, and `mise x` resolves `<bin>` through PATH. Two shapes make it find the wrapper itself again. (1) The tool is not actually installed in mise (an install failed or never ran): no shim exists, so the wrapper in `~/.local/bin` is the only `<bin>` on PATH, and stub and mise recurse as a fork storm. (2) A process inherited a PATH snapshot with `~/.local/bin` ahead of both the tool's install directory and `~/.local/share/mise/shims`, as in a systemd unit's `Environment=PATH=` or the child PATH Hermes gives ACP agents: with the shims directory present `mise x` leaves PATH order alone, so the wrapper re-execs itself in the same PID forever. Each iteration also runs `mise use -g`, which can silently upgrade the tool once mise's version cache expires.
problems.fix:
Stop the runaway processes:

```bash
pgrep -af "$HOME/.local/bin/"
pkill -f "$HOME/.local/bin/claude"     # repeat for the looping tool
```

Case 1, tool not installed. Install it once directly, or remove the wrapper if you do not use the tool:

```bash
mise ls --installed | grep -i omp || mise use -g github:can1357/oh-my-pi
# or: rm ~/.local/bin/omp
```

Case 2, bad PATH in a unit or app. Fix the PATH so mise's directories come before `~/.local/bin`, or drop the hardcoded `Environment=PATH=` and let the unit inherit the session environment:

```bash
systemctl --user cat <unit> | grep -n PATH
systemctl --user edit <unit>
systemctl --user daemon-reload && systemctl --user restart <unit>
```

As a local hardening reported to fix both cases, make the wrapper exec an absolute path so it can never find itself. Edit the last line of the affected wrapper from `exec mise x "gh" -- "gh" "$@"` to:

```bash
bin_path=$(mise which --tool "gh" "gh") || exit 1
exec mise x "gh" -- "$bin_path" "$@"
```

A later migration that regenerates wrappers can put the old form back, so re-check after updates.
problems.verify: `pgrep -af 'mise use -g'` stays empty while the tool is idle, and the formerly looping command under the same environment returns promptly, for example `systemctl --user restart <unit>` followed by low CPU in `top`.

problems.title: Update or upgrade an Omarchy 3 install after the master branch disappeared
problems.symptom:
On Omarchy 3 (git checkout at `~/.local/share/omarchy`), `omarchy-update` fails at the `Update Omarchy` git step, typically with git saying `Your configuration specifies to merge with the ref 'refs/heads/master' from the remote, but no such ref was fetched.` The documented path to Omarchy 4 (update first, then Omarchy To Quattro) is blocked by it. The manual install command from an existing Arch system also fails:

```
curl -fsSL https://omarchy.org/install | bash
curl: (22) The requested URL returned error: 404
```
problems.cause: Upstream's `master` branch, which Omarchy 3 checkouts track, was removed around 2026-09-14. The GitHub API now resolves `branches/master` to `quattro`, and raw URLs under `refs/heads/master` return 404. Omarchy 3's `bin/omarchy-update-git` runs `git -C $OMARCHY_PATH pull --autostash` against the tracked branch, which no longer exists. `https://omarchy.org/install` still serves `eval "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/basecamp/omarchy/refs/heads/master/boot.sh)"`, and that URL returns 404 (checked 2026-10-04). The `rc` branch still exists and carries both `bin/omarchy-update-git` and `bin/omarchy-upgrade-to-quattro`.
problems.fix:
Omarchy 3 install: point the checkout at `rc`, update, then upgrade to Quattro:

```bash
cd ~/.local/share/omarchy
git fetch origin
git switch rc
omarchy-update
omarchy-upgrade-to-quattro
```

The last step is also in the Omarchy 3 menu under Update > Omarchy To Quattro. Read the Quattro upgrade records before starting it: back up `/etc/snapper/configs/root`, and do not reboot if it prints `Upgrade incomplete - do NOT reboot.`

New install: use the Omarchy ISO. The curl installer from an existing Arch system is broken. A reporter's attempt with `OMARCHY_REF=rc` and the `rc` `boot.sh` failed at the rc mirror, and it installs Omarchy 3 that then needs the Quattro upgrade anyway.
problems.danger: The Quattro upgrade is one-way and multi-stage. It replaces the pacman configuration and the Snapper retention policy. Take a snapshot and a backup of anything important first.
problems.verify: `git -C ~/.local/share/omarchy rev-parse --abbrev-ref --symbolic-full-name '@{upstream}'` prints `origin/rc`, `omarchy-update` completes, and after the upgrade `pacman -Q omarchy` reports a 4.x package.

problems.title: Get the Omarchy 4.0.3 or 4.0.4 ISO past the logo when it hangs at boot
problems.symptom:
Booting the Omarchy 4.0.3 or 4.0.4 installer USB stops on the Omarchy logo and never reaches the installer. Pressing Esc shows:

```
sh: can't access tty; job control turned off
```

and the keyboard does nothing else. The same stick works on other machines, and an Ubuntu stick boots fine on the affected one. Reported on a TUXEDO InfinityBook Pro AMD Gen10, a Lenovo ThinkPad X9 (Core Ultra 7 258V) and a Beelink mini PC.
problems.cause: The early boot environment cannot find the USB device again when it needs to mount the live image, and drops to an emergency shell behind the splash. Reporters traced it to USB timing: fast USB 3 sticks, hubs and some ports fail, while a slower stick plugged directly into the machine succeeds. Upstream has not identified the exact mechanism, so treat the timing explanation as the reporters' diagnosis.
problems.fix:
Rewrite the ISO to a different, slower USB stick (USB 2.0 is fine), plug it directly into the machine rather than through a hub or dock, and try another port if it still hangs.

Verify the download first, comparing against the checksum published where you downloaded it:

```bash
sha256sum omarchy-*.iso
```

Identify the stick before writing. Run `lsblk` with the stick unplugged and again plugged in, and use the device that appeared (a whole disk such as `/dev/sdb`, never a partition such as `/dev/sdb1`):

```bash
lsblk -o NAME,SIZE,MODEL,TRAN
sudo dd if=omarchy-4.0.4.iso of=/dev/sdX bs=4M status=progress oflag=sync
```

Replace `omarchy-4.0.4.iso` with the file you downloaded and `/dev/sdX` with the stick. Reporters also had success writing with Raspberry Pi Imager where balenaEtcher errored on macOS.
problems.danger: `dd` overwrites the whole target device without asking. Pointing it at the wrong device, such as an internal disk, destroys that disk's data. Confirm the device with `lsblk` before running it.
problems.verify: The ISO boots past the logo into the Omarchy installer's configurator.
problems.audit_note: Issue #12773 (open) matches: TUXEDO InfinityBook Pro AMD Gen10, ThinkPad X9 258V and a Beelink, the `sh: can't access tty; job control turned off` line, and several reporters fixed it with a different stick plugged in directly, one with Raspberry Pi Imager where balenaEtcher errored on macOS. The cause is correctly marked as the reporters' diagnosis. The fix writes a raw image with dd to `/dev/sdX` with no step to identify the device and no danger, and a wrong device name destroys a disk. Fix now identifies the stick first and danger is added. The ISO file name and the hash in the release notes were not verified, so the fix uses a shell glob and points at the download page.

problems.title: omarchy update stops at a sudo password prompt even though passwordless sudo is enabled
problems.symptom:
Passwordless sudo is on, either through `omarchy sudo passwordless` or a hand-written `NOPASSWD: ALL` drop-in, and `sudo -n true` succeeds. `omarchy update -y` still stops right after "Create system snapshot" at:

```
[sudo] password for <user>:
```

With nobody at the keyboard (an agent, a VM driven over ssh, a supervised job) it sits there until sudo gives up, then fails with `sudo: a password is required` and "Something went wrong during the update!". The pre-update snapshot has already been taken, so the run did the risky half and none of the useful half. Every ordinary `sudo <command>` keeps working without a password, which is what makes it confusing.
problems.cause:
On Omarchy 4.0.4-1 `omarchy update` calls `omarchy-update-stay-awake start` straight after the snapshot. Lines 94 and 95 of `/usr/bin/omarchy-update-stay-awake` run `sudo -v` whenever stdin is a terminal, and `omarchy update` always gives itself one because it re-executes under `script -qefc`, so the branch is taken even in a fully unattended run.

`sudo -v` is governed by the sudoers option `verifypw`, whose default is `all`: validation is passwordless only if every sudoers entry that matches the user carries `NOPASSWD`. The user also matches a password-requiring entry (the `%wheel` rule, and on the reports in #9066 and #10352 a stock per-user `<user> ALL=(ALL) ALL` file), so `sudo -v` prompts even though command execution is passwordless. `omarchy sudo passwordless` writes `/etc/sudoers.d/99-omarchy-nopasswd-$USER` with `<user> ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL` and does not change `verifypw`, so it does not make `omarchy update` passwordless either. Upstream tracks this as open issue #9066 (#10352 was closed as its duplicate). The `quattro` branch has since rewritten this helper to use `sudo -n -N` inside an update sudo session, which is not in the 4.0.4 stable release.
problems.fix:
Tell sudo that one `NOPASSWD` entry is enough for `sudo -v`. This grants nothing beyond what your `NOPASSWD` rule already grants: when no `NOPASSWD` rule matches (for example after the `omarchy sudo passwordless` timer has expired), `sudo -v` asks for a password exactly as before.

**Omarchy 4 and plain Arch (same fix):** write the drop-in to a temporary file, have `visudo` check it, then install it. The file name must not contain a dot, or sudo skips it.

```sh
printf 'Defaults:%s verifypw=any\n' "$USER" > /tmp/98-verifypw
sudo visudo -cf /tmp/98-verifypw
sudo install -m 0440 -o root -g root /tmp/98-verifypw "/etc/sudoers.d/98-verifypw-$USER"
sudo visudo -c
rm /tmp/98-verifypw
```

The alternative from #10352 is to put `NOPASSWD:` on your existing per-user rule instead of adding a second file. A blanket `Defaults:<user> !authenticate` also works and is what this project's bench VMs use, but it makes every sudo call passwordless permanently, so prefer `verifypw=any` on a machine people use.

If an update is already hung at the prompt, type the password, or press Ctrl+C and rerun `omarchy update -y` once the drop-in is in place.
problems.danger: A malformed file in /etc/sudoers.d stops sudo working for everyone. Always run `visudo -cf` on the file before installing it and `visudo -c` afterwards, and keep a root shell or the root password available until `sudo -v` works again.
problems.verify:
With your NOPASSWD rule active (for example straight after `omarchy sudo passwordless`):

```sh
sudo -k
sudo -n -v && echo 'sudo -v is passwordless'
```

Then `omarchy update -y` should pass "Create system snapshot" without a `[sudo] password` prompt.

problems.title: omarchy update -y hangs with no output after the orphan list or a kernel update
problems.symptom:
`omarchy update -y` is supposed to ask nothing, but an unattended run stops and never finishes. The output ends either after an orphan list:

```
Orphan system packages
  asar
  vulkan-headers
```

or at the very end of a run that installed a new kernel or Hyprland. `/tmp/omarchy-update.log` shows a box-drawn `gum` prompt, "Remove N orphaned package(s)?" or "Linux kernel has been updated. Reboot?" / "Hyprland has been updated. Reboot?". Keystrokes sent to the process from outside are echoed rather than consumed. The packages are already installed, but the log analysis, status refresh and reboot step after the prompt never run.
problems.cause:
`omarchy update -y` exports `OMARCHY_UPDATE_UNATTENDED=1`, documented in `/usr/bin/omarchy-update` as "a promise not to ask anything". Two steps in Omarchy 4.0.4-1 ignore it:

- `/usr/bin/omarchy-update-orphan-pkgs` decides interactivity only from `[[ ! -t 0 || ! -t 1 ]]`. `omarchy-update` re-executes itself under `script -qefc`, which supplies a pseudo-terminal, so the test passes and `gum confirm --default=false "Remove N orphaned package(s)?"` waits forever (upstream #13356, also #8780).
- `/usr/bin/omarchy-update-restart` calls `gum confirm` in `confirm_reboot()` with no guard at all, whenever the running kernel has no matching `/usr/lib/modules/*/vmlinuz`, `~/.local/state/omarchy/reboot-required` exists, or the running Hyprland binary shows as `(deleted)` (upstream #8986).

The `quattro` branch has added an `OMARCHY_UPDATE_UNATTENDED` check to `confirm_reboot`, but not to the orphan step, and neither change is in 4.0.4.
problems.fix:
**To release a run that is already hung**, kill the `gum` process from another terminal or ssh session. That answers "no" and the update carries on to the end:

```sh
pgrep -a gum
pkill -x gum
```

**To keep the orphan prompt from appearing in the next unattended run**, deal with orphans before it. List them first:

```sh
pacman -Qtdq
```

Keep the ones you want by marking them explicitly installed, so they stop being orphans:

```sh
sudo pacman -D --asexplicit <package> [<package> ...]
```

Remove the rest only after reading the list:

```sh
sudo pacman -Rns <package> [<package> ...]
```

**The reboot prompt cannot be avoided on 4.0.4** after a kernel or Hyprland update. An automation that runs `omarchy update -y` should watch for it (`pgrep -x gum` after the package step) and kill `gum`, then reboot on its own schedule with `omarchy-system-reboot`.
problems.danger: `pacman -Rns` removes the packages and their unneeded dependencies. Read `pacman -Qtdq` first: build dependencies of AUR packages often show up as orphans and are needed for the next rebuild.
problems.verify: `pacman -Qtdq` prints nothing (or only packages you deliberately left), and the next `omarchy update -y` runs to the end, with `/tmp/omarchy-update.log` ending after the shell restart lines rather than at a `gum` prompt.

problems.title: Switching update channel from the menu installs a new kernel but never offers to reboot
problems.symptom:
Switching channel from the Omarchy menu (Update > Channel, or `omarchy-channel-set edge` / `stable` / `rc`) finishes without the usual "Reboot now?" choice, even though the switch replaced the kernel or Hyprland. The last lines are plain text instead of a prompt:

```
Linux kernel has been updated. Reboot? Run omarchy-system-reboot when ready.
Hyprland has been updated. Reboot? Run omarchy-system-reboot when ready.
```

The user closes the terminal, keeps working on a kernel whose modules are gone, and things like USB devices, VPN modules or a new monitor stop working until the next reboot.
problems.cause:
`omarchy-channel-set` ends by handing off to `omarchy-update -y` (line 99 of `/usr/bin/omarchy-channel-set` on 4.0.4-1). `-y` sets `OMARCHY_UPDATE_UNATTENDED=1`. On builds from the `quattro` branch (the `edge` and `dev` channels at the time of upstream #13416), `confirm_reboot()` in `omarchy-update-restart` checks exactly that variable and prints the fallback text instead of calling `gum confirm`. The switch is launched into a real floating terminal with a person watching, so the variable suppresses the one question that mattered.

On the stable 4.0.4-1 package `confirm_reboot()` does not check the variable, so the reboot prompt still appears after a channel switch there. The fault therefore shows when switching to or between edge builds, or once a stable release picks up the `quattro` change.
problems.fix:
After any channel switch, check by hand whether a reboot is needed.

```sh
uname -r                          # the running kernel
ls /usr/lib/modules/              # the installed kernels
ls ~/.local/state/omarchy/reboot-required 2>/dev/null && echo 'reboot marker set'
readlink /proc/$(pgrep -x Hyprland)/exe   # ends in (deleted) if Hyprland was replaced
```

If the running kernel has no directory under `/usr/lib/modules/`, the marker exists, or Hyprland shows `(deleted)`, save your work and reboot:

```sh
omarchy-system-reboot
```

Switching to or from `dev` always sets the marker (`omarchy-state set reboot-required` in `omarchy-channel-set`), so always reboot after those two.
problems.verify: After the reboot, `uname -r` matches a directory in `/usr/lib/modules/`, `~/.local/state/omarchy/reboot-required` is gone, and `omarchy-channel-current` reports the channel you chose.

problems.title: A script that shadows an omarchy command works over ssh but never runs from the desktop
problems.symptom: I copied an Omarchy command to `/usr/local/bin/omarchy-<name>` (or `~/.local/bin/omarchy-<name>`) and edited it. From ssh or a TTY my version runs. From a terminal opened in Hyprland, from a keybinding, or from the Omarchy menu, the stock version still runs and my change has no effect. `which omarchy-<name>` in a desktop terminal prints `/usr/share/omarchy/bin/omarchy-<name>`. A copy in `~/.local/bin` is never used anywhere.
problems.cause:
Omarchy 4's Hyprland config puts the Omarchy bin directory first on the session's `PATH`. `/usr/share/omarchy/default/hypr/envs.lua` (lines 30 to 36 on 4.0.4-1) removes `$OMARCHY_PATH/bin` from wherever it is in `PATH`, inserts it at position 1, and exports the result with `hl.env("PATH", ...)`. Every process Hyprland starts, including terminals, keybindings and the menu, inherits a `PATH` that begins with `/usr/share/omarchy/bin`, ahead of `/usr/local/bin`. On 4.0.4 that directory holds a symlink for almost every `omarchy-*` command (pointing at `/usr/bin/omarchy-*`), so the stock command wins.

Outside the desktop the order is different. `/etc/security/pam_env.conf` sets `PATH DEFAULT=/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:@{HOME}/.local/share/mise/shims:@{HOME}/.local/bin`, and `/usr/share/omarchy/default/bash/env-bootstrap` only prepends the Omarchy bin directory when `OMARCHY_PATH` is not `/usr/share/omarchy` (a dev link). So over ssh `/usr/local/bin` comes before `/usr/bin` and an override there works. `~/.local/bin` is appended after `/usr/bin` by both PAM and `env-bootstrap`, so a copy there loses to `/usr/bin/omarchy-*` in every context.
problems.fix:
**Recommended:** do not shadow the stock name. Give your script its own name and point the binding or hook at it, so an Omarchy update can never silently bypass it:

```sh
install -Dm755 /usr/bin/omarchy-<name> ~/.local/bin/my-<name>
$EDITOR ~/.local/bin/my-<name>
```

Then bind it in `~/.config/hypr/bindings.lua` with `hl.bind(...)` and `hl.dsp.exec_cmd("my-<name>")`, using the same form as the existing bindings in that file.

**If you must shadow the name for the whole desktop session,** use a dedicated directory that holds only your overrides, and put it first after Omarchy's defaults have loaded. Add this at the end of `~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua`, which is read after `require("default.hypr.omarchy")`:

```lua
hl.env("PATH", os.getenv("HOME") .. "/.local/omarchy-overrides/bin:" .. (os.getenv("PATH") or "/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin"))
```

```sh
mkdir -p ~/.local/omarchy-overrides/bin
mv /usr/local/bin/omarchy-<name> ~/.local/omarchy-overrides/bin/   # or copy it there
```

Log out and back in so every process starts from the new environment. Keep `~/.local/bin` itself out of that line: it holds the mise wrappers, and changing where they sit relative to mise's own directories is what makes them exec-loop (upstream #13040).

Whether `os.getenv("PATH")` at that point already reflects the `hl.env` call in `envs.lua` has not been confirmed, so check the result with the verify step rather than assuming it.

**Plain Arch with your own Hyprland config:** nothing reorders `PATH` for you, and an override in `/usr/local/bin` wins as usual.
problems.danger: A shadowed omarchy command is no longer updated by `omarchy update`. When upstream changes the stock script, your copy keeps the old behaviour, and other Omarchy scripts that call it by name will run your copy.
problems.verify:
Open a new terminal from the desktop and run:

```sh
echo "$PATH" | tr ':' '\n' | head -3
command -v omarchy-<name>
```

The override directory should be first and `command -v` should print your copy. Trigger the binding or menu entry and confirm your change takes effect.

problems.title: 'Unknown Omarchy command: omarchy debug' from a desktop terminal
problems.symptom:
Running the diagnostic the bug template and the Omarchy skill ask for fails from a terminal opened in Hyprland:

```
$ omarchy debug --no-sudo --print
Unknown Omarchy command: omarchy debug --no-sudo --print
```

The exit status is 127. `omarchy upload log <file>` and `omarchy debug idle` fail the same way, and none of them appear in `omarchy commands --all`. The same command can work over ssh, and `omarchy-debug --no-sudo --print` with a hyphen always works.
problems.cause:
The `omarchy` dispatcher (`/usr/bin/omarchy`) only discovers subcommands in its own directory: `OMARCHY_BIN_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)`, then globs `"$OMARCHY_BIN_DIR"/omarchy-*`. On 4.0.4-1 `/usr/share/omarchy/bin/` holds a symlink to `/usr/bin/` for every command except five: `omarchy-debug`, `omarchy-debug-idle` and `omarchy-upload-log` (installed to `/usr/bin` by the `omarchy-settings` package) and `omarchy-nvim-refresh` / `omarchy-nvim-setup`.

Which directory the dispatcher sees depends on how `omarchy` was found. In a Hyprland session `envs.lua` puts `/usr/share/omarchy/bin` first on `PATH`, so `omarchy` resolves to the symlink `/usr/share/omarchy/bin/omarchy`, the dispatcher scans that directory, and the three commands are missing. Over ssh or a TTY `omarchy` resolves to `/usr/bin/omarchy`, the dispatcher scans `/usr/bin`, and they are found. Checked on this machine: `/usr/share/omarchy/bin/omarchy commands --all` lists no debug command, `/usr/bin/omarchy commands --all` lists `omarchy debug`, `omarchy debug idle` and `omarchy upload log`. Upstream issues #7185 and #12374 are open.
problems.fix:
Call the scripts by their hyphenated names, which are on `PATH` in every context:

```sh
omarchy-debug --no-sudo --print       # writes the report and prints it
omarchy-debug-idle                    # idle, screensaver and lock diagnostics
omarchy-upload-log /tmp/omarchy-debug.log
```

Or call the dispatcher by its full path so it scans `/usr/bin`:

```sh
/usr/bin/omarchy debug --no-sudo --print
```

An agent following a skill or bug template that says `omarchy debug` should use `omarchy-debug` instead.
problems.danger: `omarchy-upload-log` sends the log to logs.omarchy.org. The debug report contains hardware details and network identifiers, so read it before uploading.
problems.verify: `omarchy-debug --no-sudo --print` prints the report and exits 0.

problems.title: omarchy update aborts with 'OMARCHY_PATH: unbound variable' after the snapshot
problems.symptom:
`omarchy update` takes its snapshot and then dies:

```
/usr/bin/omarchy-update-dev: line 7: OMARCHY_PATH: unbound variable
Something went wrong during the update!
```

It happens from `sudo omarchy update`, from a cron job or systemd timer, from a non-login zsh, or from an agent's shell, and never from a normal desktop terminal. A quieter form: the update finishes but the bar's update indicator is cleared even though updates are pending, with a stray `/usr/bin/omarchy-update-available: line 9: OMARCHY_PATH: unbound variable` in the output.
problems.cause:
Several Omarchy 4.0.4-1 scripts run under `set -euo pipefail` and read `$OMARCHY_PATH` with no default. `/usr/bin/omarchy-update-dev` line 7 is `[[ $OMARCHY_PATH != "/usr/share/omarchy" ]] || exit 0`, and `/usr/bin/omarchy-update-available` line 9 has the same test. `omarchy-update` runs `omarchy-update-dev` straight after `omarchy-update-stay-awake start`, so an unset variable aborts the update after the snapshot.

`omarchy-update-status` runs `omarchy-update-available` inside an `if`, and that script exits 1 both for "up to date" and for a crash, so the crash takes the `clear` branch and the indicator is wiped silently (upstream #8769).

`OMARCHY_PATH` is exported by `/usr/share/omarchy/default/bash/env-bootstrap`, which is sourced by `/etc/profile.d/omarchy.sh` (login shells), the bash rc chain and the uwsm session. `sudo` drops it under the default `env_reset`, a cron or timer environment never sources any of these, and a non-login zsh reads none of them because `/etc/profile.d` reaches zsh only through `/etc/zsh/zprofile`, which only login shells read (upstream #12858).
problems.fix:
**Omarchy 4:** run the update from a context that has `OMARCHY_PATH`, and never through `sudo`. The script calls sudo itself for the steps that need root.

```sh
bash -lc 'omarchy update'
```

or set it explicitly for one run:

```sh
OMARCHY_PATH=/usr/share/omarchy omarchy update
```

For zsh, make every zsh (login or not) pick up the same environment by adding this to `~/.zshenv`:

```sh
[ -r /usr/share/omarchy/default/bash/env-bootstrap ] && . /usr/share/omarchy/default/bash/env-bootstrap
```

For a systemd user unit or timer that runs Omarchy commands, add `Environment=OMARCHY_PATH=/usr/share/omarchy` to the `[Service]` section, or run the command with `bash -lc`.

If the indicator was cleared, refresh it once the variable is set:

```sh
OMARCHY_PATH=/usr/share/omarchy omarchy-update-status
```

**Plain Arch:** not applicable, these scripts only exist on Omarchy.
problems.verify:
```sh
env -u OMARCHY_PATH bash -lc 'echo $OMARCHY_PATH'   # prints /usr/share/omarchy
```

and `omarchy update` gets past the step after "Create system snapshot".

problems.title: omarchy update aborts with 'Refusing to use an unsafe Omarchy update inhibitor state path' on a non-English locale
problems.symptom:
`omarchy update` aborts right after "Create system snapshot", then prints the same line again from its cleanup:

```
Refusing to use an unsafe Omarchy update inhibitor state path.
Something went wrong during the update!
```

No packages are updated, and every retry fails the same way. The machine uses a non-English locale such as `pt_BR.UTF-8`, `fr_FR.UTF-8` or `zh_CN.UTF-8`. `/run/user/1000` is `drwx------` and owned by the user, so nothing is actually unsafe.
problems.cause:
The hardened `omarchy-update-stay-awake` on the `quattro` branch walks the parent chain of `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` in `root_owned_parent_chain()` and runs `stat -Lc '%u %a %F'`, then compares the third field to the English word `directory`. `stat`'s `%F` is translated through gettext, so it prints `diretório`, `répertoire` or `目录` instead, the comparison fails for `/`, and the script calls `fail_state_boundary`. The directory test a few lines earlier (`[[ -d $parent && ! -L $parent ]]`) already covers what `%F` was checking.

This code is on `quattro` (edge and dev channels, reports #13320, #13385, #13892, #14087). One report (#13376) names 4.0.4-1, but the `omarchy-update-stay-awake` shipped in the stable `omarchy 4.0.4-1` package checked on this machine contains no `root_owned_parent_chain` at all. An open pull request, #13352, forces the C locale for the call.
problems.fix:
Run the update with the C locale for messages. This changes only the language of command output for that one run:

```sh
LC_ALL=C omarchy update
```

From the menu, open a terminal and run that instead of Update > Omarchy until a release carrying the fix lands. To check whether your installed helper has the locale-dependent test:

```sh
grep -n "stat -Lc '%u %a %F'" /usr/bin/omarchy-update-stay-awake
```

A match means you need the workaround. Do not "fix" it by loosening permissions on `/run/user/$UID`: the check is right to refuse a world-writable path, and the directory is already correct.
