**3. Replace the prebuilt driver with the DKMS one.** `nvidia-open-dkms` conflicts with `nvidia-open`, so pacman asks to remove it. Answer yes. Headers must be present for every installed kernel:

```bash
sudo pacman -S --needed linux-omarchy-headers linux-headers
sudo pacman -S nvidia-open-dkms
dkms status
```

`dkms status` must show the driver `installed` for both the `-arch` and the `-omarchy` kernel. The transaction's `90-mkinitcpio-install` hook rebuilds both UKIs. If it printed `skipping.` for either kernel, follow the migration-1789325478 record.

**4. Reboot and pick the default (`linux-omarchy`) entry.**
problems.verify: On `linux-omarchy`: `uname -r` ends in `-omarchy`, `modinfo -F filename nvidia` prints a path under `/usr/lib/modules/7.2.5-3-omarchy/updates/dkms/`, `nvidia-smi` lists the GPU, and the session stays up past login.
problems.danger: Installing `nvidia-open-dkms` from a sync database newer than the installed `nvidia-utils` produces a kernel and userspace version mismatch (`NVRM: API mismatch`). Run `omarchy update` first. Do not remove the stock `linux` kernel until `linux-omarchy` has booted with a working NVIDIA driver.

problems.title: Out-of-tree and DKMS modules on linux-omarchy: build against linux-omarchy-headers, not kernel.org or Arch sources
problems.symptom:
One of these after moving to the `linux-omarchy` kernel:

- A module you compiled yourself (a patched `amdgpu`, a Wi-Fi or touchpad driver) loads, its version string matches, and the machine hangs early in boot or black-screens before the LUKS prompt. The same module rebuilt for stock `linux` worked.
- DKMS refuses to build:

```
Error! Your kernel headers for kernel 7.2.5-3-omarchy cannot be found at /usr/lib/modules/7.2.5-3-omarchy/build or /usr/lib/modules/7.2.5-3-omarchy/source.
```

- The DKMS build compiles every object, then fails at the BTF step:

```
libbpf: failed to get e_shstrndx from /usr/lib/modules/7.2.5-3-omarchy/build/vmlinux
Failed to parse base BTF '/usr/lib/modules/7.2.5-3-omarchy/build/vmlinux': -4001
make[5]: *** [.../Makefile.modfinal:52: nvidia.ko] Error 255
```
problems.cause:
`linux-omarchy` is its own kernel build. It carries patches the stock Arch kernel does not (issue 12281 traces a speaker regression to `pkgbuilds/linux-omarchy/0512-sound-fixes.patch`) and a different `.config`. On this workstation `linux-omarchy 7.2.5-3` has `CONFIG_INTEL_IOMMU_DEFAULT_ON=y` and `CONFIG_ARCH_MMAP_RND_BITS=32` where `linux 7.2.3-arch1-3` has the option unset and 28. A module built from plain kernel.org 7.2.5 sources can carry a matching version string, so `modprobe` accepts it, while its view of kernel structures differs from the running kernel. The issue 12119 reporter found exactly that on an iMac18,3 and withdrew an earlier IOMMU diagnosis once they tested the two causes apart.

DKMS builds against `/usr/lib/modules/<version>/build`, which only exists when the matching `linux-omarchy-headers` is installed. Migration `1789325478.sh` installs the headers, and migration `1789444024.sh` adds them on installs where an earlier path skipped them, but that second migration is blocked if the first one failed.

The BTF failure (issue 12856) means the `vmlinux` under `build/` is truncated on that machine. `vmlinux` belongs to `linux-omarchy-headers`, not `linux-omarchy`, and the Omarchy kernel maintainer could not reproduce it. On this workstation the same `7.2.5-3` file has intact `.BTF` and `.BTF_ids` sections, so a locally damaged headers file is the likely cause (not confirmed).
problems.fix:
**1. Headers must match the kernel exactly.**

```bash
pacman -Q linux-omarchy linux-omarchy-headers     # same version on both lines
ls -l /usr/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/build          # must exist
```

If headers are missing, install them, then let DKMS build for that kernel:

```bash
sudo pacman -S --needed linux-omarchy-headers
sudo dkms autoinstall -k 7.2.5-3-omarchy
dkms status
```

**2. Hand-built modules: build against the running kernel's tree**, never against a kernel.org or Arch source checkout:

```bash
make -C /usr/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/build M="$PWD" modules
```

If a driver project only offers "build against kernel X.Y sources", use its DKMS package instead, so it rebuilds against `linux-omarchy-headers` on every kernel update.

**3. BTF error: check the headers package, then reinstall it from the cache** (installing from the sync database could pull headers newer than the installed kernel):

```bash
readelf -S /usr/lib/modules/7.2.5-3-omarchy/build/vmlinux | grep BTF
pacman -Qkk linux-omarchy-headers
sudo pacman -U /var/cache/pacman/pkg/linux-omarchy-headers-7.2.5-3-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst
sudo dkms autoinstall -k 7.2.5-3-omarchy
```

Use the version `pacman -Q linux-omarchy` reports. A healthy `vmlinux` lists `.BTF` and `.BTF_ids` and `readelf` prints no `Error:` line.

**4. Rebuild the UKI** if the module is in the initramfs (NVIDIA early KMS, for example):

```bash
sudo limine-mkinitcpio linux-omarchy
```
problems.verify: `dkms status` shows `installed` for the `-omarchy` kernel. `modinfo -F vermagic <module>` begins with the output of `uname -r`. The machine boots `linux-omarchy` with the module loaded (`lsmod | grep <module>`).
problems.danger: Forcing a mismatched module in with `modprobe --force-vermagic` can crash the kernel or corrupt data. Do not use it to get past a version mismatch. Keep the stock `linux` entry available until a hand-built module is proven on `linux-omarchy`.

problems.title: linux-omarchy boots to a black screen, emergency shell or dead device because it turns Intel IOMMU on by default
problems.symptom:
After 4.0.4 switches the default to `linux-omarchy 7.2.5-3`, on some Intel machines (Intel Macs with AMD graphics, the 11-inch MacBook Air, Surface Pro 4, some NVIDIA desktops, an AX210 Wi-Fi laptop):

- black screen while `amdgpu` initialises, or a hang after the graphical session starts
- an initramfs emergency shell because the internal SSD never appears:

```
ERROR: device '/dev/mapper/omarchy_root' not found. Skipping fsck.
You are now being dropped into an emergency shell.
```

- touchscreen, Wi-Fi or GPU dead for the whole boot

The kernel log (when one survives) has DMA remapping faults:

```
DMAR: [DMA Read NO_PASID] Request device [0000:01:00.0] fault addr 0x77a00000 [fault reason 0x0c] non-zero reserved fields in PTE
amdgpu 0000:01:00.0: GPU Recovery Failed: -110
```

The stock `linux` entry in the Limine menu boots the same machine normally.
problems.cause:
The two kernels differ in one IOMMU option. Confirmed on this workstation:

```
linux-omarchy 7.2.5-3 : CONFIG_INTEL_IOMMU_DEFAULT_ON=y
linux 7.2.3-arch1-3   : # CONFIG_INTEL_IOMMU_DEFAULT_ON is not set
```

With VT-d translation on, every device's DMA goes through the IOMMU. Firmware whose DMAR tables omit reservations for some devices (Apple's declare an RMRR for the iGPU only), or controllers with an unlisted DMA alias quirk (the Toshiba AHCI controller `1179:010b` in MacBookAir6,1, for which a kernel quirk was sent upstream on 2026-09-29), get their DMA rejected. The device then fails: the SSD never identifies, the GPU ring times out, the Wi-Fi card raises a fatal PCIe error. AMD CPUs are not affected by this option. Not every report in these threads is this cause: the iMac18,3 reporter in issue 12119 later found an incorrectly built out-of-tree module was the real fault and IOMMU was harmless there.
problems.fix:
**Confirm first.** Boot the stock `linux` entry from the Limine menu, then read the failed boot's log if it has one:

```bash
journalctl --list-boots
journalctl -k -b -1 | grep -E 'DMAR:.*fault|iommu'
```

If there are no logs (the root never mounted), the test below is the confirmation.

**Turn the Intel IOMMU off.** Kernel parameters live inside the UKI, so put them in a drop-in, never in `/boot/limine.conf`. Use the `default` key, which both kernels receive. On stock `linux` it changes nothing, since that kernel already leaves the IOMMU off:

```bash
echo 'KERNEL_CMDLINE[default]+=" intel_iommu=off"' | sudo tee /etc/limine-entry-tool.d/zz-intel-iommu-off.conf
sudo limine-entry-tool --get-cmdline linux-omarchy | tail -n 1
```

The printed line must still contain your `root=` (or `cryptdevice=`) parameters and end with `intel_iommu=off`. Then rebuild the UKIs and Limine entries:

```bash
sudo limine-update
```

Power off fully, then boot `linux-omarchy`. A Surface Pro 4 reporter needed a full power-off, not a reboot, to recover the wedged touch controller.

Issue 12550 reports `KERNEL_CMDLINE[linux-omarchy]+=" intel_iommu=off"` in `/etc/default/limine` working too. The limine-entry-tool documentation says a kernel-specific key replaces `default` for that entry, so check that kernel's `--get-cmdline` output before rebooting if you use that form.

**Remove it** once a fixed kernel ships:

```bash
sudo rm /etc/limine-entry-tool.d/zz-intel-iommu-off.conf
sudo limine-update
```
problems.verify: On `linux-omarchy`: `grep -o intel_iommu=off /proc/cmdline` prints it, `ls /sys/kernel/iommu_groups | wc -l` prints `0`, `journalctl -k -b | grep -c 'DMAR:.*fault'` prints `0`, and the SSD, GPU, Wi-Fi or touchscreen works.
problems.danger: `intel_iommu=off` removes DMA protection against malicious Thunderbolt or PCIe devices and disables VFIO GPU passthrough. On the MacBookPro11,5 reports, booting with the IOMMU on produced Btrfs `corrupt` counter increments on the internal SSD, so stop booting `linux-omarchy` on such a machine until the parameter is in place and run `sudo btrfs scrub start -B /` afterwards. A drop-in using `=` in place of `+=` replaces the whole command line and leaves the UKI without `root=`, which cannot boot.

problems.title: linux-omarchy is installed but uname -r still shows the stock kernel (Direct Boot points at the old UKI)
problems.symptom:
The 4.0.4 update installed `linux-omarchy`, the migration finished, the Limine menu lists `linux-omarchy` first, and after any number of reboots:

```
$ uname -r
7.2.3-arch1-3
$ pacman -Q linux linux-omarchy
linux 7.2.3.arch1-3
linux-omarchy 7.2.5-3
```

Nothing reports an error. The Limine menu may never appear at all.
problems.cause:
Before the migration there was one UKI, `/boot/EFI/Linux/omarchy_linux.efi`, overwritten on each kernel update. `limine-mkinitcpio-install` names UKIs `<CUSTOM_UKI_NAME>_<kernel package>.efi`, so `linux-omarchy` gets a second file, `omarchy_linux-omarchy.efi`, and the old one stays because `linux` stays installed. Omarchy's Setup > Direct Boot (`omarchy-setup-direct-boot`) creates a firmware boot entry named `Omarchy` that loads a UKI directly and skips Limine. The migration only changes `BOOT_ORDER`, which is a Limine setting, so a Direct Boot entry keeps loading `omarchy_linux.efi` (issue 12145, reproduced on an AMD desktop and an Intel Lenovo laptop). Re-running `omarchy-setup-direct-boot` does not reliably fix it either, because it picks the UKI with `find ... -name "omarchy*.efi" | head -1`, whose order is not defined.

Issue 12664 reports a second cause: the shipped template `/usr/share/omarchy/default/limine/limine.conf` sets `default_entry: 2`. Limine's documentation counts a directory as an entry, so in a menu that opens with the `/+Omarchy` directory, index 2 normally selects the first kernel under it, which is `linux-omarchy`. The 12664 reporter saw the stock kernel selected anyway. That cause is unconfirmed.
problems.fix:
**1. Find which path booted you.**

```bash
uname -r
efibootmgr | grep -E 'BootCurrent|BootOrder|Omarchy|Limine'
sudo limine-entry-tool --tree
```

If `BootCurrent` matches an `Omarchy` entry ending in `\EFI\LINUX\OMARCHY_LINUX.EFI`, Direct Boot is the cause.

**2. Point Direct Boot at the Omarchy kernel's UKI.** Remove the old entry by running the menu script as your user (it calls sudo itself and asks to remove an existing entry):

```bash
omarchy-setup-direct-boot
```

Then create the new entry by hand with the explicit filename, using the disk and partition number of your ESP:

```bash
findmnt -n -o SOURCE /boot          # for example /dev/nvme0n1p1 means disk /dev/nvme0n1, part 1
sudo efibootmgr --create --disk /dev/nvme0n1 --part 1 --label "Omarchy" --loader '\EFI\Linux\omarchy_linux-omarchy.efi'
efibootmgr                          # the new Omarchy entry should be first in BootOrder
```

Or turn Direct Boot off for good (step 2's script, answer yes, and skip the `--create`) so Limine and `BOOT_ORDER` decide.

**3. Without Direct Boot**, watch which entry the Limine menu highlights at power-on. If it highlights `linux`, check the default line:

```bash
sudo grep -nE '^(default_entry|remember_last_entry)' /boot/limine.conf
```

Limine accepts a path in place of an index (`default_entry: Omarchy/linux-omarchy`, matching the names `limine-entry-tool --tree` printed). Editing `/boot/limine.conf` this way is untested here: `omarchy-refresh-limine` copies the template back over it.
problems.verify: After a reboot with no key pressed, `uname -r` ends in `-omarchy`. With Direct Boot, `efibootmgr -v` shows `BootCurrent` on the entry whose path is `\EFI\Linux\omarchy_linux-omarchy.efi`.
problems.danger: A wrong `--disk` or `--part` creates a firmware entry that cannot boot. The Limine entry stays in the firmware boot menu as a way back, so note its `Boot####` number before changing anything and do not delete it.

problems.title: Hardware broke after 4.0.4 moved you to linux-omarchy: make the stock linux kernel the default again
problems.symptom: Since the Omarchy 4.0.4 update (which installed `linux-omarchy 7.2.5-3` and made it the first Limine entry), something works only on the stock kernel: the machine resets before the LUKS prompt, freezes, loses Wi-Fi, touchpad, backlight, HDMI audio or suspend. Picking `linux` in the Limine menu at every boot fixes it until you forget.
problems.cause: Migration `1789325478.sh` installs `linux-omarchy` and writes `BOOT_ORDER="linux-omarchy, linux-omarchy-*, *, *fallback, Snapshots"` to `/etc/default/limine`, which `limine-entry-tool` reads last and which overrides every drop-in. It deliberately keeps stock `linux` installed "so it remains available if the new one cannot boot". The upstream tracker has many hardware-specific regressions reported against `linux-omarchy 7.2.5-3` that stock `linux 7.2.3` does not show. Its exemption covers T2 Macs only (`linux-t2` or a `-t2` kernel), so T1 and older Macs were switched too (issue 12281). The migration exits early once `/var/lib/omarchy/migrations/1789325478` exists, so it never rewrites `BOOT_ORDER` again.
problems.fix:
**1. Put `linux` first in `/etc/default/limine`.** Editing `/etc/limine-entry-tool.d/omarchy-defaults.conf` does nothing here, because `/etc/default/limine` overrides it.

```bash
sudoedit /etc/default/limine
```

Replace the `BOOT_ORDER=` line with:

```
BOOT_ORDER="linux, linux-omarchy, linux-omarchy-*, *, *fallback, Snapshots"
```

Leave the `ESP_PATH` and `KERNEL_CMDLINE` lines alone.

**2. Regenerate the Limine entries.**

```bash
sudo limine-update
sudo limine-entry-tool --tree        # linux should now be listed first
```

**3. If Direct Boot is enabled** (`efibootmgr | grep Omarchy`), the firmware entry decides, not Limine. Make it point at `\EFI\Linux\omarchy_linux.efi`, as in the record on the stock kernel still booting.

**4. Keep `linux-omarchy` installed** so you can retest a later release from the menu. One beta report (issue 12087, Beelink SER9) was fixed by a firmware update alone, so check for a BIOS update and retest. An Intel machine whose failure shows `DMAR:` faults may only need `intel_iommu=off` (see that record) rather than the stock kernel.

To return to the Omarchy kernel later, put `linux-omarchy` first again and rerun `sudo limine-update`.
problems.verify: Reboot without touching the menu. `uname -r` prints the `-arch` version and the broken device works.
problems.danger: Stock `linux` must stay installed and its DKMS modules built (`dkms status`) for this to work. A mistyped `BOOT_ORDER` only reorders entries, but deleting the `KERNEL_CMDLINE` line from `/etc/default/limine` removes `root=` from every UKI on the next rebuild and nothing boots.

problems.title: The ESP fills up after the linux-omarchy migration: two kernels plus snapshot copies, and the update checks only /
problems.symptom:
Since the 4.0.4 update `df -h /boot` keeps climbing. Then one of these: snapshot entries stop appearing in the Limine menu, a kernel update ends with a write error from the UKI hook, or the machine no longer boots its normal entry. `omarchy update` never warned. A reporter's 2 GB ESP held:

```
834M  /boot/EFI/Linux
  280M  omarchy_linux.efi
  277M  recovery20260920_linux-omarchy.efi
  277M  recovery20260920_linux.efi
277M  /boot/<machine-id>/limine_history/omarchy_linux.efi_sha256_...
```
problems.cause: With `ENABLE_UKI=yes` (Omarchy's `omarchy-uki.conf`) each installed kernel package gets its own UKI in `/boot/EFI/Linux/`, named `omarchy_<package>.efi`. The migration keeps stock `linux` and adds `linux-omarchy`, so ESP demand for current kernels doubles. `limine-snapper-sync` also stores the kernel files of each snapshot under `/boot/<machine-id>/limine_history/`, deduplicated by hash, so each distinct kernel version costs another copy, and a UKI carrying NVIDIA modules and GPU firmware can exceed 250 MB. `limine-snapper-sync` stops adding entries at `LIMIT_USAGE_PERCENT=85`, which still allows the ESP to fill to 85 percent. `omarchy-update-requires-free-space` checks only `/` for 10 GiB (identical in 4.0.4 and `quattro`), and the UKI is written by the `90-mkinitcpio-install` hook after the pacman transaction has committed. Issue 11821 traced that `limine-entry-tool` copies with replace-existing, which unlinks the old UKI first, so running out of space part way through leaves that kernel with no UKI at all.
problems.fix:
**1. See what is using the ESP.** `/boot` is mounted `dmask=0077`, so listing it needs root:

```bash
df -h /boot
sudo du -h --max-depth=3 /boot | sort -h | tail -15
sudo ls -lhS /boot/EFI/Linux/
limine-snapper-list
sudo limine-snapper-info
```

**2. Remove the kernel you do not boot.** If `linux-omarchy` works on this machine, removing stock `linux` halves the current-kernel cost. Follow the record on removing the unused stock kernel, which lists the checks to do first.

**3. Remove old snapshot entries** (the IDs come from `limine-snapper-list`):

```bash
sudo limine-snapper-remove 1..2
```

**4. Keep fewer entries from now on.** Put settings in `/etc/default/limine`, which is read after every drop-in. A drop-in such as `98-*.conf` sorts before `omarchy-defaults.conf` and is overridden by its `MAX_SNAPSHOT_ENTRIES=6`.

```bash
sudoedit /etc/default/limine
```

```
MAX_SNAPSHOT_ENTRIES=4
```

If you keep both kernels, the `EXCLUDE_SNAPSHOT_ENTRIES` setting documented in `/etc/limine-snapper-sync.conf` can keep the stock kernel out of new snapshot entries. Its patterns match entry names, so `EXCLUDE_SNAPSHOT_ENTRIES="linux"` should match only the entry named `linux`. That is untested here, so check `sudo limine-entry-tool --tree` after the next snapshot.

```bash
sudo limine-update
sudo limine-snapper-sync
```

**5. Before each update until this is fixed upstream**, check the ESP yourself:

```bash
df -h /boot      # keep free space above the size of your largest UKI plus a margin
```

The lasting fix is a larger ESP. limine-snapper-sync recommends at least 4 GiB, and Arch suggests 8 GiB when booting Snapper snapshots from Limine. Resizing means repartitioning from a live USB with a full backup.
problems.verify: `df -h /boot` shows free space well above one UKI's size, `sudo limine-snapper-info` reports no missing or corrupt kernels, and the next `omarchy update` prints no `skipping.` line from the UKI hook.
problems.danger: Never delete files in `/boot/EFI/Linux/` or `limine_history` by hand. Use `limine-snapper-remove` and package removal, which also update `limine.conf`. Do not reboot after a UKI hook failed for lack of space until `sudo limine-mkinitcpio` completes without `skipping.`. Repartitioning the ESP can destroy data.

problems.title: Remove the unused stock linux kernel that sits beside linux-omarchy (and whose entry can get booted by mistake)
problems.symptom: The machine runs `linux-omarchy`, yet `pacman -Q linux` shows the stock kernel still installed and the Limine menu still lists a `linux` entry. Fresh 4.0.4 installs have it too. One reporter booted it by accident three weeks after installing, on a kernel version they had never run, and blamed it for a Btrfs failure. Others just see the ESP filling and kernel updates taking twice as long, since every update rebuilds two UKIs and two sets of DKMS modules.
problems.cause: Two paths leave stock `linux` in place. The upgrade migration `1789325478.sh` keeps it on purpose as an escape hatch. Fresh installs get it from the archinstall base package set (`'linux'` appears in the installer's package list in `/var/log/archinstall/install.log` per issue 13537), even though Omarchy's own package lists name `linux-omarchy`. `limine-entry-tool` creates an entry for every installed kernel, so a never-updated-by-use kernel stays one keypress away. The Btrfs corruption attribution in issue 13537 was made by an agent-filed report and is not confirmed. limine-snapper-sync's own documentation does warn that switching often between kernel versions raises the risk of filesystem breakage.
problems.fix:
**1. Check it is safe.** All of these must hold:

```bash
uname -r                                   # must end in -omarchy
pacman -Qi linux | grep 'Required By'      # prebuilt module packages show here
dkms status                                # DKMS modules built for the -omarchy kernel
pacman -Q linux-t2 2>/dev/null             # T2 Macs use linux-t2: stop here if present
```

If `Required By` names a prebuilt module package such as `nvidia-open`, switch it to its DKMS variant first (see the prebuilt nvidia-open record). If this machine needed stock `linux` because of a `linux-omarchy` regression, keep it.

**2. Remove the stock kernel and its headers.** `pacman -R` is not blocked by Omarchy's guard, which only stops `-S` combined with `-u`:

```bash
sudo pacman -R linux linux-headers
```

The `60-limine-mkinitcpio-remove-pre` and `90-limine-mkinitcpio-remove-post` hooks remove its Limine entry and its UKI. If pacman refuses because another package requires `linux`, read the package it names before going further. `linux-omarchy` provides `NTSYNC-MODULE`, `WIREGUARD-MODULE`, `KSMBD-MODULE` and `VIRTUALBOX-GUEST-MODULES`, which should satisfy packages depending on those.

**3. Check the result.**

```bash
sudo limine-entry-tool --tree
sudo ls /boot/EFI/Linux/
df -h /boot
```
problems.verify: `pacman -Q linux` reports it is not installed, the Limine menu lists only `linux-omarchy` (plus snapshots), and a reboot lands in `uname -r` ending in `-omarchy`.
problems.danger: Omarchy 4 has no fallback initramfs entry. After removal, the only bootable kernel is `linux-omarchy` plus older snapshot entries, so a future `linux-omarchy` regression on your hardware needs a snapshot or a live USB to recover. Keep an Omarchy or Arch USB stick. Never remove the kernel you are currently running.

problems.title: Limine snapshot entries start the stock kernel, and rolling back past 4.0.4 removes linux-omarchy for good
problems.symptom: After the kernel migration you open the Limine Snapshots submenu to roll back, and the snapshot entries only offer `linux`, not `linux-omarchy`. Or you restored a snapshot from before the 4.0.4 update, ran `omarchy update` afterwards, and `linux-omarchy` never came back: `pacman -Q linux-omarchy` says it is not installed and the menu shows only the stock kernel.
problems.cause:
`limine-snapper-sync` adds each snapshot entry "with its matching kernel versions", meaning the kernels installed inside that snapshot's root, with their files kept under `/boot/<machine-id>/limine_history/`. `omarchy update` takes its snapshot (`omarchy-snapshot create`) before `omarchy-update-system-pkgs` installs anything, so the snapshot made by the very update that ran migration 1789325478 does not contain `linux-omarchy`. On this workstation all three snapshot entries are dated before the migration ran (2026-09-18 12:50 against a migration marker at 12:55), so every one of them boots a stock kernel. Only snapshots taken by later updates contain both kernels.

Restoring a pre-migration snapshot rolls back `@`, which holds the package database, `/etc/default/limine` and the machine-wide marker `/var/lib/omarchy/migrations/1789325478`. It does not roll back `@home`, which holds the per-user marker `~/.local/state/omarchy/migrations/1789325478.sh`. `omarchy-migrate` decides by the per-user marker, so it never reruns the migration, and the `omarchy` package does not depend on `linux-omarchy`, so no update reinstalls it. This follows from reading `omarchy-migrate`, `omarchy-update` and the migration on 4.0.4. A real restore was not exercised.
problems.fix:
**See which kernels a snapshot entry carries** before booting it:

```bash
limine-snapper-list
sudo limine-entry-tool --tree 4
```

Entries under a snapshot are named after the kernel packages it contains. A snapshot entry for `linux` boots that snapshot's root with the stock kernel, which is the right pairing for a snapshot taken before the migration.

**After restoring a pre-4.0.4 snapshot, bring the Omarchy kernel back** by clearing your per-user markers for the two kernel migrations and rerunning the update as your user:

```bash
ls ~/.local/state/omarchy/migrations/ | grep -E '1789325478|1789444024'
rm ~/.local/state/omarchy/migrations/1789325478.sh ~/.local/state/omarchy/migrations/1789444024.sh
omarchy update
```

The migration then installs `linux-omarchy` and its headers again, rewrites `BOOT_ORDER` and rebuilds its UKI. If it stops with "The Omarchy kernel has no Limine boot entry", follow that record.

If you restored that snapshot on purpose because `linux-omarchy` broke your hardware, leave the markers alone. You are already on the stock kernel.
problems.verify: `pacman -Q linux-omarchy` shows it installed, `sudo limine-entry-tool --tree` lists it first, and after a reboot `uname -r` ends in `-omarchy`. Snapshots created by the next `omarchy update` list both kernels.
problems.danger: Delete only the two marker files named. Removing the whole `migrations` directory replays every Omarchy migration since install, some of which rewrite your configuration.

problems.title: omarchy update fails with thousands of "linux: /usr/lib/modules/<version>/... exists in filesystem" conflicts
problems.symptom:
`omarchy update` aborts before installing anything, with thousands of lines like:

```
error: failed to commit transaction (conflicting files)
linux: /usr/lib/modules/7.1.9-arch1-2/... exists in filesystem
```

and the generic "Something went wrong during the update!" screen. Every retry fails the same way.
problems.cause: Omarchy installs `kernel-modules-hook`. Its `10-linux-modules-post` hook copies the running kernel's module tree back into `/usr/lib/modules/` after any kernel install or upgrade so the live system keeps loading modules. When a kernel package goes backwards to an older version (a release migration downgraded `linux` from 7.1.9 to 7.1.8 in issue 9142) and you do not reboot, the running version's tree stays on disk owned by no package. When the repository later offers that version again, pacman's file conflict check, which runs before any hook, finds every file already present. `linux-modules-cleanup.service` skips the running kernel's tree, so the wedge persists for as long as you stay booted into it. Omarchy's conflict handler (`omarchy-update-system-pkgs-when-conflicted`) only clears unowned files reported against `omarchy` or `omarchy-settings` packages in 4.0.4 and on `quattro`. PR 9285, which would handle this case, is still open.
problems.fix:
**1. Confirm the conflicting tree is unowned leftovers of the running kernel.** Use the version from the error lines:

```bash
uname -r
pacman -Qo /usr/lib/modules/7.1.9-arch1-2     # "No package owns" confirms it
```

**Option A, the safer one: reboot into the installed kernel.** Then `linux-modules-cleanup.service` moves the now non-running tree to `/usr/lib/modules/.old/` at boot:

```bash
sudo reboot
# after the reboot
ls /usr/lib/modules/
omarchy update
```

**Option B, without rebooting:** let pacman take ownership of that one tree in a full upgrade. Scope `--overwrite` to the exact directory from the error, then run the normal update so migrations and hooks still run:

```bash
sudo env OMARCHY_ALLOW_DIRECT_PACMAN=1 pacman -Syu --overwrite '/usr/lib/modules/7.1.9-arch1-2/*'
omarchy update
```

The issue 9142 reporter compared the on-disk files with the cached package using `diff -rq` before overwriting and found them identical.
problems.verify: `pacman -Qo /usr/lib/modules/$(uname -r)` names the kernel package, and `omarchy update` completes without conflicting-file errors.
problems.danger: Never use a broad `--overwrite '*'` or `--overwrite '/usr/*'`: it silently replaces files other packages own. Option B's `-Syu` bypasses Omarchy's update entrypoint for that one transaction, which is why `omarchy update` must follow it.

problems.title: Limine panics with "efi: LoadImage failure" on the Omarchy UKI (older UEFI, or Secure Boot on MSI boards)
problems.symptom:
Limine shows its menu, you pick Omarchy, and it halts:

```
PANIC: efi: LoadImage failure (0x8000000000000002)
Stacktrace: <panic+...> <chainload+...> <boot+...> <_menu+...>
End of trace. System halted.
```

`0x8000000000000002` (`EFI_INVALID_PARAMETER`) was reported on a fresh install on a Bay Trail ThinkPad Yoga 11e. `0x800000000000000f` (`EFI_ACCESS_DENIED`) was reported with Secure Boot enabled on an MSI X870E board, even with the UKI signed by `sbctl`. The kernel never starts.
problems.cause: Omarchy ships `/etc/limine-entry-tool.d/omarchy-uki.conf` with `ENABLE_UKI=yes`, overriding the package template's `ENABLE_UKI=no`, so each kernel becomes a UKI that Limine starts with `protocol: efi`, through the firmware's `LoadImage()` call. Some firmware rejects that: older UEFI implementations with `EFI_INVALID_PARAMETER`, and MSI firmware with Secure Boot on with `EFI_ACCESS_DENIED` (the reporter linked sbctl's FQ0001 firmware quirk). With `ENABLE_UKI=no`, `limine-mkinitcpio-install` builds a plain kernel and initramfs under `/boot/<machine-id>/<kernel>/` and Limine loads them itself with `protocol: linux`, never calling `LoadImage()`. This is a different fault from the stale `arch-linux.efi` entry panic, which reads `Failed to open image`.
problems.fix:
Get a shell on the installed system: from a working entry, or by chrooting from the Omarchy ISO (mount all four subvolumes `@ @home @log @pkg` and the ESP at `/mnt/boot` first, see the chroot record).

**1. Turn UKIs off in `/etc/default/limine`**, not in `omarchy-uki.conf`, which `omarchy-settings` owns and overwrites on update:

```bash
echo 'ENABLE_UKI=no' | sudo tee -a /etc/default/limine
```

**2. Rebuild the boot files and entries.**

```bash
sudo limine-update
sudo grep -n 'protocol:' /boot/limine.conf     # kernel entries should now say protocol: linux
```

Inside an `arch-chroot`, run `limine-update` without `sudo`.

**3. Reboot** and pick the normal entry.

With Secure Boot on, the MSI reporter booted cleanly from then on. The Bay Trail reporter had generated the `protocol: linux` entry but had not yet confirmed a full boot.
problems.verify: The machine boots past Limine, and `sudo grep -c 'protocol: efi' /boot/limine.conf` no longer counts the kernel entries (other EFI chainload entries, such as Windows, may remain).
problems.danger: Snapshot entries created before the change still point at UKIs in `limine_history` and panic the same way if selected, so a rollback has to use a snapshot made after the change. Chroot without mounting the ESP at `/mnt/boot` and `limine-update` writes to the root filesystem instead of the ESP.

problems.title: Raise a laptop NVIDIA GPU stuck at its base power limit by enabling nvidia-powerd
problems.symptom: Games run far worse than on Windows or CachyOS on the same NVIDIA laptop. `nvidia-smi` shows the card pinned at its default limit under full load, for example `Pwr:Usage/Cap 49W / 50W`, while `nvidia-smi -q -d POWER` lists a higher `Max Power Limit` it never reaches. Temperatures stay low, which makes it look like a hardware or driver fault. Some Proton games also log `SuspendThread loop failed` on exit.
problems.cause: NVIDIA Dynamic Boost, the mechanism that lets a laptop GPU draw more than its base TGP, is not automatic on Linux. It needs the userspace daemon `nvidia-powerd`, which ships in `nvidia-utils` as `nvidia-powerd.service` with preset disabled, so nothing starts it unless the installer or the user enables it. Omarchy 4's `install/hardware/nvidia.sh` installs the driver and writes the modprobe and mkinitcpio files but never enables the service (confirmed on 4.0.4-1 by grepping `/usr/share/omarchy` for `powerd`, which returns nothing). Without the daemon the GPU stays at its Default Power Limit. omarchy#9678 reproduced it both ways on an RTX 5060 Laptop: 50 W with the daemon masked, 85 to 93 W with it running. Requirements per the Arch wiki: Ampere or newer GPU, Intel Comet Lake or AMD Renoir or newer platform, and firmware-level Dynamic Boost support.
problems.fix:
Check whether the platform supports Dynamic Boost and whether the daemon runs:

```bash
cat /proc/driver/nvidia/gpus/*/power
systemctl status nvidia-powerd
nvidia-smi -q -d POWER | grep -i 'power limit'
```

Enable it. This is the same on Omarchy 4 and plain Arch, since the unit comes from `nvidia-utils` (or `nvidia-580xx-utils` on the legacy branch, which predates Ampere and so does not apply):

```bash
sudo systemctl enable --now nvidia-powerd
```

Some laptops only expose the higher limit in a firmware or vendor performance mode (the Arch wiki names some Lenovo Legion models). On an ASUS machine with `asusctl` installed, select the performance profile as well.

On a desktop card the daemon finds nothing to manage, so enabling it there changes nothing.
problems.verify: Under load, `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=power.draw,power.limit --format=csv -l 2` shows `power.limit` above the Default Power Limit and draw climbing past the old cap. `systemctl is-enabled nvidia-powerd` prints `enabled`.

problems.title: Fix Nautilus and other GTK4 apps that exit at launch or freeze on close on NVIDIA
problems.symptom: Files (Nautilus) does nothing when launched from the menu. From a terminal it prints `Gdk-Message: Error 22 (Invalid argument) dispatching to Wayland display` and exits with status 1, and the journal says `Lost connection to Wayland compositor`. Or, on other NVIDIA machines, Nautilus and GNOME Calculator open fine but hang every time the window is closed, with no crash and nothing in dmesg.
problems.cause: GTK4 renders with its Vulkan renderer by default. Two NVIDIA failures sit on that path. On a machine where Hyprland's primary GPU is not the NVIDIA one (a second GPU, a virtio GPU in a passthrough VM) and the only Vulkan ICD is `nvidia_icd.json`, GTK renders on the NVIDIA card and hands explicit-sync dmabufs to a compositor rendering on the other GPU, and Hyprland drops the client (omarchy#12622, reproduced on Omarchy 4.0.4-1, gtk4 4.22.4, nvidia-open 610.57.04). Separately, the close-time hang reported in omarchy#883 was an NVIDIA 580 driver regression, which a commenter on that issue says NVIDIA fixed in 580.82.07. In both cases the GL renderer avoids the failing path. Omarchy 4.0.4 sets no `GSK_RENDERER` (confirmed by grepping `/usr/share/omarchy`).
problems.fix:
Confirm the renderer is the trigger with a one-off launch. Quit any running Nautilus first, because a new launch otherwise hands off to the existing instance and the variable never applies:

```bash
nautilus -q
GSK_RENDERER=ngl nautilus --new-window
```

If that works, set it for the session.

**Omarchy 4** (Lua config). Add this to `~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua` below the `require("default.hypr.omarchy")` line. Do not put it in a new `~/.config/hypr/envs.lua`, because the stock `hyprland.lua` never requires that file (omarchy#9902):

```lua
-- GTK4: use the GL renderer instead of Vulkan on NVIDIA
hl.env("GSK_RENDERER", "ngl")
```

Log out and back in so every app inherits it.

**Plain Arch with hyprlang** (`~/.config/hypr/hyprland.conf`):

```
env = GSK_RENDERER,ngl
```

**Only one app:** copy its desktop file, prefix the command, and turn off D-Bus activation. Nautilus ships `DBusActivatable=true`, and a launcher that honours it starts Nautilus through its D-Bus service and ignores the `Exec` line:

```bash
mkdir -p ~/.local/share/applications
cp /usr/share/applications/org.gnome.Nautilus.desktop ~/.local/share/applications/
sed -i -e 's|^Exec=nautilus|Exec=env GSK_RENDERER=ngl nautilus|' \
       -e 's|^DBusActivatable=true|DBusActivatable=false|' \
       ~/.local/share/applications/org.gnome.Nautilus.desktop
nautilus -q
```

Nautilus can still be started by D-Bus without the variable, for example when another app asks it to show a folder. If that happens, use the session-wide setting instead.

If only the close-time hang occurs and the driver is a 580 release older than 580.82.07, updating the driver is the real fix.
problems.verify: `nautilus --new-window` opens and closes cleanly. In a new terminal, `echo $GSK_RENDERER` prints `ngl`.
problems.audit_note: Cause and session-wide fix hold. omarchy#12622 has the exact Gdk-Message, the VM setup, the version list and a table showing GSK_RENDERER=gl/ngl/cairo working. omarchy#883 carries the comment that NVIDIA bug 5436037 was fixed in 580.82.07. grep for GSK_RENDERER in /usr/share/omarchy returns nothing on 4.0.4-1, hl.env is the documented Lua call (Hyprland wiki environment-variables page, and Omarchy's own default/hypr/nvidia.lua uses it), and omarchy#9902 confirms envs.lua is never loaded. The defect is in the one-off test and the per-app branch: /usr/share/applications/org.gnome.Nautilus.desktop on this machine has DBusActivatable=true and /usr/share/dbus-1/services/org.gnome.Nautilus.service starts '/usr/bin/nautilus --gapplication-service'. A launcher that honours DBusActivatable ignores Exec, so the sed edit can do nothing, and if a Nautilus instance is already running both the test command and the edited Exec just forward to it without the variable. The fix now quits the running instance first and turns D-Bus activation off in the copied file. Not exercised: no NVIDIA multi-GPU setup here.

problems.title: Stop the mouse cursor outline turning bright blue when nightlight is on (NVIDIA)
problems.symptom: On an NVIDIA GPU, as soon as nightlight is turned on (`omarchy toggle nightlight`), the mouse pointer's outline turns fluorescent blue while the rest of the screen is warm-tinted. With nightlight off the cursor looks normal.
problems.cause: Omarchy's nightlight runs hyprsunset, which applies a colour transform matrix (CTM). With hardware cursors, the cursor is drawn on a separate hardware plane, and on the NVIDIA driver that plane does not receive the CTM, so the cursor stays untinted and its edges render blue against the transformed image. Reported on Omarchy 4.0.4-1, Hyprland 0.56.2, hyprsunset 0.4.0-3, nvidia-open 610.57.04 (omarchy#13912). A commenter there links an NVIDIA forum report of the same behaviour under KDE Plasma, so it is at least partly driver-side. Software cursors are drawn into the frame and do get tinted.
problems.verify: Toggle nightlight on with `omarchy toggle nightlight` and the cursor is tinted like the rest of the screen, with no blue outline.

problems.title: Recover an AMD desktop that hard-freezes seconds after login since ddcutil 3.0.0
problems.symptom:
Right after an update, every login freezes the whole machine 2 to 12 seconds after Hyprland starts. Mouse, keyboard and Ctrl+Alt+F2 are dead and only a hard reset works. After a reboot, `journalctl -k -b -1` shows:

```
ddcutil[2344]: (i2c_ioctl_reader1) Error in ioctl() read, rc=-1, errno=EIO(-5): Input/output error, device=/dev/i2c-0
amdgpu 0000:03:00.0: Failed to set workload mask 0x00000001
amdgpu 0000:03:00.0: SMU is in hanged state, failed to send smu message!
amdgpu 0000:03:00.0: Failed to disable gfxoff!
```

Reported on discrete Radeon RX 7600, 7900 XT/XTX and 9070 XT with an external monitor.
problems.cause: ddcutil 3.0.0 (Arch extra, 2026-09-12) changed how it reads EDIDs over I2C, using one multi-message ioctl. On some Radeon cards that triggered an amdgpu SMU hang. Omarchy hits it at every login on desktops with external monitors because the shell's monitor panel runs `omarchy-brightness-display-ddc`, which calls `ddcutil --skip-ddc-checks detect --brief`, and its bus cache lives in `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, so it is empty at each login and `detect` always runs (omarchy#11499, with an A/B on ddcutil 2.2.7 versus 3.0.0). KDE PowerDevil users hit the same thing through libddcutil. Upstream released 3.0.1 to replace 3.0.0, and 3.0.2 (2026-09-23) disabled the multi-message EDID read, saying it may have triggered the amdgpu crash. Arch extra carried 3.0.2-1 when this was written.
problems.fix:
You need a working system without the graphical session running long enough to change the package.

**Omarchy 4: boot a snapshot from before the update.** At the Limine menu open the Snapshots submenu and boot the snapshot taken before the update that brought in ddcutil 3.0.0. Then make it permanent and update again, which now pulls a fixed ddcutil:

```bash
sudo limine-snapper-restore
# reboot into the restored system, then:
pacman -Q ddcutil
omarchy update
```

**Plain Arch, or if you can get a shell another way** (ssh from another machine, or a live USB plus `arch-chroot`): check the version and move off 3.0.0.

```bash
pacman -Q ddcutil
# Plain Arch: a full upgrade brings 3.0.2 or later
sudo pacman -Syu
# Omarchy 4: the ALPM guard refuses -Syu, use
omarchy update
```

If a 3.0.x release still freezes your card, downgrade to 2.2.7 from the Arch archive and hold it:

```bash
sudo pacman -U https://archive.archlinux.org/packages/d/ddcutil/ddcutil-2.2.7-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst
sudo sed -i 's/^#\?IgnorePkg *=.*/IgnorePkg = ddcutil/' /etc/pacman.conf
grep '^IgnorePkg' /etc/pacman.conf
```

Check that `IgnorePkg` line by eye: if you already held other packages, add `ddcutil` to the existing list instead of replacing it.
problems.verify: `pacman -Q ddcutil` shows 3.0.2 or later (or the held 2.2.7). Two or three logins in a row stay responsive, and `journalctl -k -b | grep -i 'SMU is in hanged state'` returns nothing.
problems.danger: Restoring a snapshot rolls back every package and system file changed since it was taken. Holding a package with IgnorePkg leaves it behind future upgrades. Remove the hold once a fixed release works for you, or the downgraded ddcutil can drift out of step with its libraries.

problems.title: Boot the Arch kernel when an AMD display broke after Omarchy 4.0.4 switched to linux-omarchy 7.2.5
problems.symptom:
After the update to Omarchy 4.0.4 and a reboot, an AMD machine's display misbehaves in one of these ways: a 4K monitor over HDMI goes black for 2 to 5 seconds every time the screen changes after being still (typing, moving the mouse), a 4K@120 HDMI monitor gets no signal at all, the LUKS prompt is black so you unlock blind, or a monitor behind a USB-C dock is detected but stays black at `0x0` in `hyprctl monitors`. The kernel log shows lines such as:

```
amdgpu 0000:66:00.0: [drm] enabling link 1 failed: 19
[drm:dcn20_wait_for_blank_complete [amdgpu]] *ERROR* DC: failed to blank crtc!
amdgpu 0000:07:00.0: [drm] enabling link 2 failed: 15
WARNING: ... at fill_dc_mst_payload_table_from_drm+0x191/0x1a0 [amdgpu]
```

`uname -r` prints `7.2.5-3-omarchy`.
problems.cause: Omarchy 4.0.4 migration `1789325478.sh` installs `linux-omarchy` and `linux-omarchy-headers` and rewrites `BOOT_ORDER` in `/etc/default/limine` to `"linux-omarchy, linux-omarchy-*, *, *fallback, Snapshots"`, so the machine boots the Omarchy kernel first while the old Arch `linux` kernel stays installed. `linux-omarchy 7.2.5-3` carries amdgpu display regressions relative to Arch `linux 7.2.3.arch1-3`: HDMI link training failures at high bandwidth on DCN 3.1.4 and DCN 3.2 (omarchy#12083) and a DP MST link enable failure behind docks (omarchy#13119). Multiple reporters confirmed that booting the Arch kernel on the same install fixes it. A 7.2.7rc1 test build fixed the MST case on one machine and did not fix the HDMI case on another, so a newer Omarchy kernel is not yet a confirmed fix. `/etc/default/limine` is loaded last by `limine-common-functions`, so its `BOOT_ORDER` beats every drop-in.
problems.fix:
**1. Boot the Arch kernel once.** At the Limine menu pick the plain `linux` entry instead of `linux-omarchy`. After login:

```bash
uname -r                       # want ...-arch..., not ...-omarchy
pacman -Q linux linux-omarchy
```

If `linux` is not installed, install it with headers, which DKMS drivers such as `nvidia-open-dkms` need:

```bash
sudo pacman -S --needed linux linux-headers
```

**2. Make it the default.** Edit the `BOOT_ORDER` line in `/etc/default/limine` so `linux` comes first, then rebuild the boot entries (`limine-update` runs `limine-mkinitcpio` itself):

```bash
sudo sed -i -E 's/^[[:space:]]*BOOT_ORDER[[:space:]]*=.*/BOOT_ORDER="linux, linux-omarchy, linux-omarchy-*, *, *fallback, Snapshots"/' /etc/default/limine
grep BOOT_ORDER /etc/default/limine
sudo limine-update
```

Leave `linux-omarchy` installed so you can switch back when a fixed release lands. The migration that set the order is guarded by `/var/lib/omarchy/migrations/1789325478`, so it does not run again and reset your order.

**3. Watch the Arch kernel version.** Reporters confirmed the fix on Arch `linux 7.2.3.arch1-3`. The next `omarchy update` upgrades `linux` too, and newer Arch kernels have not been tested against this bug. One reporter placed the regression between 7.2.3 and 7.2.5, so it may be upstream rather than Omarchy-specific. After each update:

```bash
pacman -Q linux
```

If the display fault returns on a newer Arch kernel, boot the Limine snapshot from before that update and report the version on omarchy#12083 or #13119.

**Stopgap for the HDMI blanking only**, if you must stay on the Omarchy kernel: drop the monitor to 60 Hz in `~/.config/hypr/monitors.lua`. Reporters saw this hold at 4K@60 on DCN 3.2, but on DCN 3.1.4 4K@60 still failed at early boot:

```lua
hl.monitor({ output = "HDMI-A-1", mode = "3840x2160@60", position = "auto", scale = 1.6, vrr = 0 })
```

This does not apply to plain Arch, which never installs `linux-omarchy`.
problems.verify: After a reboot with no menu interaction, `uname -r` shows the Arch kernel, the monitor holds its mode, and `journalctl -k -b | grep -E 'enabling link .* failed|fill_dc_mst_payload'` returns nothing.
problems.danger: Changing the boot order changes which kernel boots unattended. Keep at least two kernels installed, and do not remove `linux-omarchy` and `linux` in the same transaction, or you can be left with no bootable kernel.
problems.audit_note: The mechanism is confirmed on this machine. /usr/share/omarchy/migrations/1789325478.sh installs linux-omarchy and its headers, deletes and re-appends BOOT_ORDER in /etc/default/limine as stated, leaves the old kernel installed, and is guarded by /var/lib/omarchy/migrations/1789325478. /usr/lib/limine/limine-common-functions loads /etc/default/limine last ('highest priority'). This workstation runs 7.2.5-3-omarchy with linux 7.2.3.arch1-3 installed. omarchy#12083 and #13119 back the symptoms, the DCN 3.1.4 and 3.2 findings, the black LUKS prompt, 4K@60 failing early on DCN 3.1.4, and 7.2.7rc1 fixing MST on Krackan while not fixing HDMI. The hl.monitor syntax matches Omarchy's config/hypr/monitors.lua. The gap: core/linux is now 7.2.8.arch1-2 (archlinux.org JSON, 2026-10-02), so the next omarchy update moves the Arch kernel off the 7.2.3 that reporters tested. One #12083 reporter places the regression between 7.2.3 and 7.2.5, which suggests it could be upstream and in newer Arch kernels too. Nobody has tested that. The fix now tells the reader to check which Arch kernel they are booting and what to do if the problem comes back. Also, limine-update itself calls limine-mkinitcpio (read from /usr/bin/limine-update), so either command alone rebuilds the entries. Not exercised: no boot order was changed.

problems.title: Remove NVIDIA userspace pulled onto an AMD or Intel-only machine, which hijacks OpenGL and EGL
problems.symptom: A machine with no NVIDIA GPU has `nvidia-utils` and `lib32-nvidia-utils` installed, and odd graphics failures follow: Brave or Chromium's GPU process crashes repeatedly (backtrace through `libnvidia-egl-wayland2.so.1` and `libEGL_nvidia.so.0`) until the browser drops to software rendering, Minecraft or PrismLauncher dies with `Driver does not support OpenGL 3.3`, or Omarchy's Install > AI > Ollama menu installs `ollama-cuda` and about 3 GB of CUDA on an AMD card. `nvidia-smi` exists but says `NVIDIA-SMI has failed because it couldn't communicate with the NVIDIA driver`.
problems.cause: `nvidia-utils` provides the virtual `opengl-driver` and `vulkan-driver`, and `lib32-nvidia-utils` provides `lib32-vulkan-driver`. `steam` depends on `lib32-vulkan-driver`, and under `--noconfirm` pacman takes the first provider, `lib32-nvidia-utils`, which hard-depends on `nvidia-utils`. On Omarchy 4, `omarchy-install-gaming-steam` installs `steam` before its GPU-aware `omarchy-install-gaming-gpu-lib32` step, so AMD machines get the NVIDIA stack (omarchy#8856, #12392). Once installed, `nvidia-utils` ships `/usr/share/glvnd/egl_vendor.d/10_nvidia.json`, which libglvnd tries before Mesa's `50_mesa.json`, so EGL context creation goes to the NVIDIA libraries first. The Ollama menu entry in `default/omarchy/omarchy-menu.jsonc` picks `ollama-cuda` whenever the `nvidia-smi` command exists, which is true here (omarchy#10380, still the case in 4.0.4).
problems.fix:
Confirm there is no NVIDIA hardware and see what pulled the packages in:

```bash
lspci | grep -iE 'vga|3d|display'
pacman -Qi nvidia-utils lib32-nvidia-utils | grep -E '^(Name|Required By|Install Reason)'
ls /usr/share/glvnd/egl_vendor.d/
```

Install the Mesa providers for your GPU FIRST, so the virtual dependencies stay satisfied:

```bash
# AMD
sudo pacman -S --needed mesa lib32-mesa vulkan-radeon lib32-vulkan-radeon
# Intel
sudo pacman -S --needed mesa lib32-mesa vulkan-intel lib32-vulkan-intel
```

Then remove the NVIDIA userspace. Preview it first:

```bash
sudo pacman -Rsp lib32-nvidia-utils nvidia-utils
sudo pacman -Rs lib32-nvidia-utils nvidia-utils
```

If pacman refuses because some package still needs a provider, read which one and install its Mesa equivalent rather than forcing with `-Rdd`. Leave `linux-firmware-nvidia` alone: the `linux-firmware` meta package depends on it.

If the Ollama menu installed `ollama-cuda` on an AMD card, swap the backend:

```bash
sudo pacman -Rns ollama-cuda
sudo pacman -S --needed ollama-vulkan     # or ollama-rocm
```

Fully quit and restart the browser. Chromium's fall-back to software rendering after repeated GPU process crashes lasts only for that run, so a normal restart clears it once the NVIDIA libraries are gone. Check `chrome://gpu` (or `brave://gpu`) afterwards.
problems.verify: `pacman -Q nvidia-utils` reports not found, `ls /usr/share/glvnd/egl_vendor.d/` shows only `50_mesa.json`, `glxinfo -B | grep renderer` (from `mesa-utils`) names radeonsi or Intel, and `chrome://gpu` in Chromium shows hardware acceleration enabled.
problems.danger: Do not run this on a machine that has an NVIDIA GPU, including a hybrid laptop whose dGPU is powered off and missing from a quick look: check `lspci` first. Removing the only Vulkan or OpenGL provider breaks Hyprland and Steam, so install the Mesa packages before removing anything.
problems.audit_note: The cause is confirmed. pacman -Si shows nvidia-utils provides vulkan-driver and opengl-driver, lib32-nvidia-utils provides lib32-vulkan-driver and depends on nvidia-utils=610.57.04, and steam depends on lib32-vulkan-driver. /usr/share/omarchy/bin/omarchy-install-gaming-steam runs omarchy-pkg-add steam before omarchy-install-gaming-gpu-lib32. /usr/share/glvnd/egl_vendor.d/ holds 10_nvidia.json and 50_mesa.json. The install.ai.ollama entry in default/omarchy/omarchy-menu.jsonc picks ollama-cuda whenever nvidia-smi is present. linux-firmware 20260810-2 depends on linux-firmware-nvidia. omarchy#8856, #12392 and #10380 all exist, are open, and support the claims. ollama-vulkan and ollama-rocm are in Arch extra. One line was wrong: --ignore-gpu-blocklist overrides Chromium's static driver blocklist and does not clear anything. Chromium's switch to software after repeated GPU process crashes lasts only for that browser run, so a normal restart once the NVIDIA libraries are gone is what clears it. Not exercised: no packages were removed.

problems.title: Stop the Omarchy shell holding the NVIDIA dGPU awake on a hybrid laptop
problems.symptom: On an Intel or AMD plus NVIDIA laptop whose session renders on the iGPU, battery drains fast even at idle. `nvidia-smi` lists no processes, yet `cat /sys/bus/pci/devices/0000:01:00.0/power/runtime_status` stays `active`. `sudo fuser -v /dev/nvidia0 /dev/nvidiactl` shows `quickshell` holding about 19 handles alongside Hyprland.
problems.cause: The Omarchy shell is Quickshell. Constructing a Qt Multimedia `MediaPlayer` (the lock-explorer plugin creates one eagerly for its unlock clip) makes Qt's FFmpeg backend enumerate hardware encode and decode devices at shell start, which opens `/dev/nvidia0`, `/dev/nvidiactl`, `/dev/nvidia-uvm`, `/dev/nvidia-modeset` and a render node. Open handles block runtime D3, so the dGPU never suspends (omarchy#12506, Omarchy 4.0.4, quickshell 0.3.1). Stopping the shell alone let the GPU suspend within about 15 seconds on the reporter's machine. Setting Qt's FFmpeg hardware device lists to empty stops the probing. This is a different holder from apps rendering on the dGPU, which the record `nvidia-dgpu-no-runtime-d3-battery-drain` covers along with the RTD3 setup itself.
problems.fix:
Confirm the shell is the holder:

```bash
sudo fuser -v /dev/nvidia*
cat /sys/bus/pci/devices/0000:01:00.0/power/runtime_status   # adjust the PCI address from lspci
```

Disable Qt's FFmpeg hardware backends for the session. In `~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua`, below `require("default.hypr.omarchy")`:

```lua
-- Keep Qt Multimedia from opening the NVIDIA dGPU at shell start
hl.env("QT_FFMPEG_DECODING_HW_DEVICE_TYPES", ",")
hl.env("QT_FFMPEG_ENCODING_HW_DEVICE_TYPES", ",")
```

The shell is started by `omarchy-launch-shell` from Hyprland's start hook and inherits `hl.env` values, so log out and back in to apply it.

This affects Qt apps only: their video decode falls back to software. Browsers and mpv are unaffected.
problems.verify: After logging back in, `sudo fuser -v /dev/nvidia*` no longer lists `quickshell`, and within about 15 seconds `runtime_status` reads `suspended`.

problems.title: Fix supergfxd hanging after 'omarchy toggle hybrid gpu' switches to Integrated mode
problems.symptom:
After `omarchy toggle hybrid gpu`, choosing integrated only and rebooting, the toggle now says `supergfxd is not responding. Try again, or check: systemctl status supergfxd`. `timeout 5 supergfxctl -g` exits 124. HDMI outputs wired to the dGPU are gone but the battery still drains, `systemctl reboot` or suspend can hang, and the journal shows:

```
INFO: task supergfxd:1022 blocked for more than 122 seconds.
 snd_card_free+0x7a/0xa0 [snd]
 unbind_store+0xa4/0xb0
```
problems.cause: In Integrated mode supergfxd removes the NVIDIA modules and unbinds both PCI functions of the dGPU, including its HDMI audio function (`0000:01:00.1`, driver `snd_hda_intel`). `snd_card_free` waits for the last reference to the ALSA card, and WirePlumber, which starts with the session at the same moment, has just opened it. `supergfxd.service` is `Type=dbus`, so systemd counts it started once it owns its bus name, and the mode change runs afterwards, during session startup. Omarchy's `delay-start.conf` (`ExecStartPre=/bin/sleep 5`) only moves the collision later (omarchy#10445, HP Victus, Omarchy 4.0.2 and 4.0.4). A later comment found a second holder: Quickshell and Firefox reloading the NVIDIA module through GLVND after supergfxd removed it. A wedged supergfxd ignores SIGKILL.
problems.fix:
**Get out of the wedged state.** The daemon cannot be killed. Hold the power button, boot, and before the toggle runs again switch the config back to Hybrid from a terminal:

```bash
sudo sed -i 's/"mode": ".*"/"mode": "Hybrid"/' /etc/supergfxd.conf
sudo rm -f /usr/lib/systemd/system-sleep/force-igpu /etc/systemd/system/supergfxd.service.d/delay-start.conf
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo reboot
```

Those are exactly the files `omarchy-toggle-hybrid-gpu` removes when it switches back to Hybrid.

**To keep Integrated mode working** (community workaround from omarchy#10445, not an Omarchy fix). Detach the dGPU audio function as soon as it binds at boot, before WirePlumber exists. Find its address with `lspci -D | grep -i 'nvidia.*audio'` and use it in both files:

```bash
sudo tee /etc/udev/rules.d/90-ignore-nvidia-hdmi-audio.rules >/dev/null <<'EOF'
ACTION=="bind", SUBSYSTEM=="pci", KERNEL=="0000:01:00.1", DRIVER=="snd_hda_intel", RUN+="/usr/local/bin/detach-nvidia-hdmi-audio"
EOF
sudo tee /usr/local/bin/detach-nvidia-hdmi-audio >/dev/null <<'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
grep -Eq '"mode"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"(Integrated|Vfio)"' /etc/supergfxd.conf || exit 0
echo 0000:01:00.1 > /sys/bus/pci/drivers/snd_hda_intel/unbind
EOF
sudo chmod 755 /usr/local/bin/detach-nvidia-hdmi-audio
```

The same commenter, on an AMD iGPU machine, also had to stop the session loading NVIDIA's EGL and VDPAU libraries. In `~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua`, below `require("default.hypr.omarchy")`:

```lua
hl.env("__EGL_VENDOR_LIBRARY_FILENAMES", "/usr/share/glvnd/egl_vendor.d/50_mesa.json")
hl.env("VDPAU_DRIVER", "radeonsi")
```

`VDPAU_DRIVER=radeonsi` fits an AMD iGPU only. Leave it out on Intel. The EGL line keeps every EGL app off the NVIDIA GPU, so remove both lines before switching back to Hybrid, or offloaded EGL apps will not use the dGPU.

Then run `omarchy toggle hybrid gpu` again.
problems.verify: After the reboot into Integrated mode, `timeout 5 supergfxctl -g` prints `Integrated` immediately, `journalctl -b -u supergfxd` contains `Reloaded gfx mode: Integrated`, and `journalctl -k -b | grep 'blocked for more than'` is empty.
problems.danger: A wedged supergfxd needs a forced power-off, which can lose unsaved work. The PCI address is machine-specific: a wrong one in the udev rule unbinds a different device.
problems.audit_note: The cause, symptom and escape procedure hold. /usr/share/omarchy/bin/omarchy-toggle-hybrid-gpu on 4.0.4-1 prints the quoted 'supergfxd is not responding' message, and its Integrated-to-Hybrid branch runs the same sed and removes the same two files (force-igpu and delay-start.conf). omarchy#10445 (open) has the snd_card_free/unbind_store stack, the HP Victus 4.0.4-1 report, the second holder (NVIDIA module reloaded through GLVND), the SIGKILL note, and the udev rule and script the record reproduces word for word. One gap: the commenter set __EGL_VENDOR_LIBRARY_FILENAMES to Mesa only, session-wide. That also stops EGL apps from using the NVIDIA GPU in Hybrid mode, so it has to come back out before switching back to Hybrid. VDPAU_DRIVER=radeonsi applies to an AMD iGPU only, and the commenter notes Mesa 26 ships no VDPAU driver, so the setting just turns VDPAU off. The corrected fix adds both caveats. Not exercised: no supergfxd machine here.

problems.title: Fix choppy 60 fps bar and menu animations on NVIDIA high-refresh monitors
problems.symptom: On an NVIDIA GPU with a 144 Hz or 240 Hz monitor, Hyprland's window animations are smooth but everything the Omarchy shell draws (bar, tray drawer, menus, OSDs) moves at about 60 fps and looks choppy. Some NVIDIA users also see the lock screen crash with `QWaylandGLContext::makeCurrent: eglError: 0x3003` followed by `FATAL: Failed to initialize graphics backend for OpenGL`.
problems.cause: Qt disables threaded OpenGL rendering on the proprietary NVIDIA driver whenever `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP` is set, as a workaround for QTBUG-95817. Qt Quick then uses its basic render loop, which drives animations from a roughly 16 ms timer with no vsync awareness, so the whole shell is capped near 60 fps. `QSG_INFO=1` reports `basic render loop` on NVIDIA and `threaded render loop` on Mesa (omarchy#7268, Omarchy 4.0.0, RTX 4090 and RTX 5080). With the Vulkan RHI backend the threaded loop is Qt's default everywhere. Omarchy 4.0.4 still sets no `QSG_RHI_BACKEND`.
problems.fix:
Run the shell on Qt's Vulkan backend. In `~/.config/hypr/hyprland.lua`, below `require("default.hypr.omarchy")`:

```lua
-- Qt Quick: Vulkan backend restores the threaded render loop on NVIDIA
hl.env("QSG_RHI_BACKEND", "vulkan")
```

Log out and back in so the shell inherits it.

Use this only when the NVIDIA GPU drives the display. On a hybrid laptop where the iGPU drives the panel, the shell already gets Mesa's threaded loop, and the issue author advises against forcing Vulkan there.
problems.verify: `tr '\0' '\n' < /proc/$(pgrep -x quickshell)/environ | grep QSG_RHI_BACKEND` prints `QSG_RHI_BACKEND=vulkan`, and shell animations look as smooth as window animations.

problems.title: Make Ollama use an AMD GPU that ROCm silently ignores
problems.symptom: Ollama answers slowly and `amdgpu_top` or `ollama ps` shows the model running on CPU (`100% CPU`) even though the machine has a Radeon card. On Omarchy, Install > AI > Ollama may also have installed plain `ollama` or `ollama-cuda` instead of a ROCm or Vulkan backend.
problems.cause: ROCm skips GPUs that are not on its supported list without an error, so `ollama-rocm` falls back to the CPU on many consumer and integrated Radeons. Separately, Omarchy's Ollama menu entry only picks `ollama-rocm` when the `rocminfo` command exists, and a stock Omarchy AMD install never has it, so AMD owners get CPU-only `ollama`, or `ollama-cuda` if `nvidia-utils` was pulled in (omarchy#10380, unchanged in 4.0.4). The Arch backends are add-on packages that depend on `ollama`: `ollama-rocm`, `ollama-vulkan` and `ollama-cuda`.
problems.fix:
**Easiest on RDNA 3 and newer: use the Vulkan backend.** The Arch wiki notes it is usually faster than ROCm there and avoids the unsupported-GPU problem. No environment variable is needed:

```bash
sudo pacman -S --needed ollama-vulkan
sudo systemctl restart ollama
```

Integrated GPUs are skipped unless you set `OLLAMA_IGPU_ENABLE=1` in the service.

**Staying on ROCm: override the GFX version.**

```bash
sudo pacman -S --needed ollama-rocm
/opt/rocm/bin/rocminfo | grep amdhsa          # e.g. gfx1103
find /opt/rocm/lib/rocblas/library -name 'Kernels.so-*'
```

Pick a version from the rocblas list whose major part equals yours and whose other parts are not higher (a 4-digit `gfx1103` reads as `11.0.3`):

```bash
sudo systemctl edit ollama
```

```ini
[Service]
Environment="HSA_OVERRIDE_GFX_VERSION=11.0.0"
```

```bash
sudo systemctl restart ollama
```

If the menu installed `ollama-cuda` on an AMD machine, remove it with `sudo pacman -Rns ollama-cuda`.
problems.verify: Run a model, then `ollama ps` shows `100% GPU` and `amdgpu_top` shows GPU load and VRAM in use. `journalctl -u ollama -b | grep -i -E 'rocm|vulkan|gfx'` names the backend and device.

problems.title: Get Ollama back on the NVIDIA GPU after suspend and resume
problems.symptom: Ollama used the NVIDIA GPU fine until the machine slept. After resume, models load on the CPU (`ollama ps` shows `100% CPU`), generation is slow, and the service log no longer lists the CUDA device. Rebooting fixes it until the next suspend.
problems.cause: Ollama's own GPU documentation describes this as an NVIDIA driver bug: after a suspend and resume cycle Ollama sometimes fails to discover the NVIDIA GPU and falls back to the CPU. The workaround it documents is reloading the NVIDIA Unified Memory module `nvidia_uvm`, which CUDA uses. On Omarchy 4, `nvidia_uvm` is loaded early from the initramfs (`/etc/mkinitcpio.conf.d/nvidia.conf`), but it can still be unloaded and reloaded at runtime once nothing holds it.
problems.fix:
Stop anything using CUDA, reload the module, restart Ollama:

```bash
sudo systemctl stop ollama
sudo rmmod nvidia_uvm
sudo modprobe nvidia_uvm
sudo systemctl start ollama
```

If `rmmod` reports `Module nvidia_uvm is in use`, find the holder and stop it first:

```bash
sudo fuser -v /dev/nvidia-uvm
```

This is the same on Omarchy 4 and plain Arch.
problems.verify: `ollama run <model> 'hi'` followed by `ollama ps` shows `100% GPU`, and `nvidia-smi` lists the `ollama` process.

problems.title: Stop an Intel laptop panel flickering by disabling Panel Self Refresh
problems.symptom: The built-in screen of an Intel laptop flickers, briefly shows stale content, or the cursor and typed text lag a frame behind when the image is otherwise still. The kernel log may show `[i915] *ERROR* CPU pipe A FIFO underrun`. External monitors are fine.
problems.cause: Panel Self Refresh (PSR, and PSR2 or Selective Update) lets the panel keep showing its last frame while the GPU link idles, to save power. On some panel and driver combinations the hand-off back to live frames misbehaves and the screen flickers. The Arch wiki lists it as a known cause and gives `i915.enable_psr=0`, or `xe.enable_psr=0` for machines on the newer `xe` driver, as the workaround, noting it can also clear the FIFO underrun error. Values are 0 to disable, 1 for up to PSR1 and 2 for up to PSR2.
problems.fix:
Find which driver runs the GPU and read the current setting:

```bash
lspci -k | grep -A3 -iE 'vga|display'      # 'Kernel driver in use: i915' or 'xe'
cat /sys/module/i915/parameters/enable_psr 2>/dev/null
cat /sys/module/xe/parameters/enable_psr 2>/dev/null
```

**Omarchy 4.** The command line is baked into the UKI, so add it in a drop-in that sorts after `omarchy-defaults.conf`, always with `+=`, and rebuild. Use the line for your driver:

```bash
sudo tee -a /etc/limine-entry-tool.d/zz-local.conf >/dev/null <<'EOF'
KERNEL_CMDLINE[default]+=" i915.enable_psr=0"
EOF
# xe driver instead: KERNEL_CMDLINE[default]+=" xe.enable_psr=0"
sudo limine-mkinitcpio && sudo limine-update
sudo reboot
```

Use `tee -a`, which keeps parameters added earlier. Do not edit `/boot/limine.conf`, which is regenerated. See the record `limine-kernel-parameters-not-applying-omarchy` for the mechanism.

**Plain Arch, GRUB:** add `i915.enable_psr=0` to `GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT` in `/etc/default/grub`, then `sudo grub-mkconfig -o /boot/grub/grub.cfg`. **systemd-boot:** append it to the `options` line in `/boot/loader/entries/*.conf`.

If full disable costs too much battery, try `enable_psr=1` (PSR1 only) instead of 0.
problems.verify: After reboot, `cat /proc/cmdline` contains the parameter, `cat /sys/module/i915/parameters/enable_psr` (or `xe`) prints `0`, and the flicker is gone. `journalctl -k -b | grep -i underrun` is empty.

problems.title: Unlock AMD GPU clock, voltage and power controls for LACT or CoreCtrl
problems.symptom: LACT or CoreCtrl shows the GPU but the overclocking, undervolting or power limit controls are greyed out or missing, or writing to `/sys/class/drm/card*/device/pp_od_clk_voltage` fails. LACT may say overclocking is not enabled.
problems.cause: amdgpu only exposes manual clock and voltage control in sysfs when the PowerPlay overdrive bit is set in the `amdgpu.ppfeaturemask` kernel parameter. The default mask leaves `PP_OVERDRIVE_MASK` (0x4000) off. The Arch wiki warns that setting all 32 bits (`0xffffffff`) can enable unstable features that cause screen flicker or broken resume, and recommends adding only 0x4000 to the default mask. On Omarchy, power-profiles-daemon 0.30 is installed and can override the amdgpu performance level, which LACT 0.7.5 and newer disables automatically.
problems.fix:
Compute a mask that adds only the overdrive bit to your current mask:

```bash
printf 'amdgpu.ppfeaturemask=0x%x\n' "$(($(cat /sys/module/amdgpu/parameters/ppfeaturemask) | 0x4000))"
```

**Omarchy 4.** Put the printed value in a drop-in and rebuild the UKI (replace the value with yours):

```bash
sudo tee -a /etc/limine-entry-tool.d/zz-local.conf >/dev/null <<'EOF'
KERNEL_CMDLINE[default]+=" amdgpu.ppfeaturemask=0xfff7ffff"
EOF
sudo limine-mkinitcpio && sudo limine-update
sudo reboot
```

If `zz-local.conf` already sets `amdgpu.ppfeaturemask` (for example the gfxoff workaround in `amdgpu-idle-freeze-gfxoff-ppfeaturemask`), edit that value in place to combine both bits rather than adding a second one.

On Omarchy, do not use LACT's own "enable overclocking" button. It sees `ID_LIKE=arch`, writes `/etc/modprobe.d/99-amdgpu-overdrive.conf` and runs `mkinitcpio -P`. Omarchy 4 has no presets in `/etc/mkinitcpio.d/`, so that rebuilds nothing, and `amdgpu` is loaded from the initramfs, so the option is not applied. If you already pressed it, remove the file so it does not end up in a later UKI with a different mask:

```bash
sudo rm -f /etc/modprobe.d/99-amdgpu-overdrive.conf
```

**Plain Arch, GRUB:** add the value to `GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT` in `/etc/default/grub` and run `sudo grub-mkconfig -o /boot/grub/grub.cfg`. On plain Arch with mkinitcpio presets, LACT's button also works.

Then install and start LACT:

```bash
sudo pacman -S --needed lact
sudo systemctl enable --now lactd
```

After the reboot, check:

```bash
cat /proc/cmdline
printf '0x%x\n' $(( $(cat /sys/module/amdgpu/parameters/ppfeaturemask) & 0x4000 ))   # 0x4000 means overdrive is on
```
problems.verify: `cat /sys/module/amdgpu/parameters/ppfeaturemask` shows the new value, `cat /sys/class/drm/card*/device/pp_od_clk_voltage` prints clock tables, and LACT's overclocking page is editable.
problems.danger: Overclocking or undervolting can cause crashes, GPU hangs and in rare cases hardware damage. Setting the full 0xffffffff mask can break suspend and resume. LACT documents recovery from a bad overclock on its wiki: keep that page handy before applying settings at boot.
problems.audit_note: The cause and the manual drop-in hold. Arch wiki AMDGPU (raw) has the 0x4000 PP_OVERDRIVE_MASK advice, the warning about 0xffffffff, and the exact printf the record uses. The LACT README says LACT 0.7.5+ with power-profiles-daemon 0.30+ disables the conflicting amdgpu action. This machine has power-profiles-daemon 0.30-1 and Arch extra has lact 0.10.1. The cross-referenced slug amdgpu-idle-freeze-gfxoff-ppfeaturemask exists. The gap is a trap on Omarchy. LACT's own 'enable overclocking' action (lact-daemon/src/system.rs, enable_overdrive) matches ID_LIKE=arch, which Omarchy's /etc/os-release has (ID=omarchy). It writes /etc/modprobe.d/99-amdgpu-overdrive.conf and then runs 'mkinitcpio -P', but /etc/mkinitcpio.d/ is empty on Omarchy 4, so there are no presets to rebuild and the option never reaches the UKI. The kms hook puts amdgpu in the initramfs, so a modprobe.d option only applies after a UKI rebuild. The corrected fix says to use the kernel-parameter drop-in and not LACT's button, and how to clean up after it. I did not run mkinitcpio -P to see how it fails.

problems.title: Diagnose 'Xid 79: GPU has fallen off the bus' crashes on NVIDIA
problems.symptom:
The screen freezes or goes black, the session dies, or the dGPU vanishes, sometimes under load and sometimes seconds after boot or at idle. `journalctl -k -b -1` shows:

```
NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:27:00): 79, GPU has fallen off the bus.
```

sometimes followed by `Xid 154: GPU Reset Required`. `nvidia-smi` then fails until a reboot.
problems.cause: Xid 79 means the driver tried to reach the GPU over PCI Express and found it inaccessible. It is a symptom with several causes, not one bug. In Arch forum threads the confirmed causes include dust and overheating, a loose or underpowered PCIe power cable, PCIe link power management (ASPM), GSP firmware on the closed driver, and on some laptops a specific power-state transition (P0 to P3 to P5) that no driver option fixed. The solved thread on a GTX 970 needed cleaning, re-seating power cables and the kernel parameters `nvidia.NVreg_EnableGpuFirmware=0 pcie_aspm=off`. An Ampere laptop thread tried `pcie_aspm=off` and both `NVreg_DynamicPowerManagement` values without success and remains unresolved.
problems.fix:
**1. Rule out hardware first.** Check temperature and power under load, clean the cooler, and re-seat the GPU and its power connectors on a desktop:

```bash
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=temperature.gpu,power.draw,pstate --format=csv -l 2
journalctl -k -b -1 | grep -E 'Xid|NVRM'
```

**2. Disable PCIe ASPM**, which helped in the solved thread.

Omarchy 4, in a drop-in that sorts after `omarchy-defaults.conf`:

```bash
sudo tee -a /etc/limine-entry-tool.d/zz-local.conf >/dev/null <<'EOF'
KERNEL_CMDLINE[default]+=" pcie_aspm=off"
EOF
sudo limine-mkinitcpio && sudo limine-update
sudo reboot
```

Plain Arch, GRUB: add `pcie_aspm=off` to `GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT` in `/etc/default/grub`, then `sudo grub-mkconfig -o /boot/grub/grub.cfg`.

**3. On the closed driver only, also try disabling GSP firmware** with `nvidia.NVreg_EnableGpuFirmware=0` added the same way. Omarchy 4 installs `nvidia-open-dkms` on GSP-capable cards, and the open modules require GSP, so this step does not apply there. See `nvidia-gsp-firmware-crashes`.

**4. Collect a report** if it persists, for NVIDIA's forum:

```bash
sudo nvidia-bug-report.sh
```
problems.verify: Several days of normal use and a sustained load test pass with no `Xid` lines in `journalctl -k`. `cat /proc/cmdline` contains the parameters you added.
problems.danger: `pcie_aspm=off` raises idle power use, noticeably on laptops. Opening a desktop case to re-seat power cables should be done with the machine unplugged.

problems.title: Stop AMD laptop panel flicker or a frozen internal screen caused by Panel Replay
problems.symptom: On a recent AMD laptop (Ryzen AI 300 "Strix Point" or "Krackan", Ryzen 7040/8040 "Phoenix" or "Hawk Point", Framework 13 or 16, ASUS Zenbook S16), the internal screen flickers, flashes brief pink or garbled frames, or freezes on the last frame shortly after the desktop or greeter appears. The machine keeps running: VT switching works, SSH works, and an external monitor plugged in during the freeze shows a picture while the laptop panel stays stuck. The usual PSR fix, `amdgpu.dcdebugmask=0x10`, changes nothing, and `amdgpu.psr=0` changes nothing either. The kernel log is usually clean at the moment it happens.
problems.cause:
Panel Replay is a newer eDP self-refresh mode, separate from Panel Self Refresh v1 and PSR Selectively Updated. amdgpu enables it when the panel advertises support. The panel keeps showing its own stored frame, and a broken entry or exit path on some panel and firmware combinations produces flicker, or a panel that never takes a new frame.

`amdgpu.dcdebugmask` is a bitmask over `enum DC_DEBUG_MASK` in `drivers/gpu/drm/amd/include/amd_shared.h`. Three bits matter here:

- `DC_DISABLE_PSR = 0x10` disables PSR v1 and PSR-SU
- `DC_DISABLE_PSR_SU = 0x200` disables PSR-SU only
- `DC_DISABLE_REPLAY = 0x400` disables Panel Replay

So `0x10`, the value most guides give, leaves Panel Replay switched on. Upstream reports match this:

- drm/amd #5519: ASUS Zenbook S16 with a Ryzen AI 9 465 (DCN 3.5) and a Samsung ATNA60HR07-0 OLED. Every 7.0.x and 7.1.x kernel froze the panel at the Wayland greeter and 6.19.14 worked. `0x10` did not help and `0x400` alone fixed it.
- drm/amd #5772: Radeon 780M IdeaPad flicker. `amdgpu.psr=0` and `0x10` did not help and `0x410` fixed it.
- drm/amd #3344: a Framework 16 flicker regression, bisected in 6.9 to the commit "drm/amd/display: Enable Panel Replay for static screen use case".

In #5561, a TUXEDO vendor kernel sets `amdgpu.dcdebugmask=0x610` by default, which is PSR, PSR-SU and Replay all off.

`amdgpu.psr` is not a parameter at all. `modinfo -p amdgpu` on kernel 7.2.5 lists `dcdebugmask`, `dcfeaturemask` and `abmlevel`, but no `psr`, so that advice is a silent no-op.
problems.fix:
**1. Confirm the panel uses Panel Replay** (root, debugfs):

```bash
sudo sh -c 'for d in /sys/kernel/debug/dri/*/eDP-*; do echo "$d"; cat "$d/replay_capability" "$d/psr_capability" 2>/dev/null; done'
```

If `replay_capability` reports the sink and driver as supported, this record applies.

**2. Pick the value.** `dcdebugmask` is one bitmask and a `0444` parameter, so it is read only at boot. If the parameter appears twice on the command line, only the last one counts. Combine bits into a single value:

| value | disables |
|---|---|
| `0x400` | Panel Replay only. Start here |
| `0x410` | Panel Replay plus PSR v1 and PSR-SU |
| `0x610` | Panel Replay, PSR and PSR-SU explicitly |

If you already carry `amdgpu.dcdebugmask=0x10` from the flip_done record, replace it with `0x410`. Do not add a second entry.

**3. Omarchy 4 (Limine + UKI).** The command line is baked into `/boot/EFI/Linux/omarchy_linux.efi`, and `/boot/limine.conf` is regenerated, so use your own drop-in that sorts after `omarchy-defaults.conf`, with `+=`:

```bash
sudo tee -a /etc/limine-entry-tool.d/zz-local.conf >/dev/null <<'EOF'
# `+=` appends. A bare `=` would wipe Omarchy's own defaults.
KERNEL_CMDLINE[default]+=" amdgpu.dcdebugmask=0x400"
EOF
sudo limine-mkinitcpio && sudo limine-update && sudo reboot
```

To test once without writing anything, see the record `limine-kernel-parameters-not-applying-omarchy`. A Limine menu edit must keep the whole existing command line, because it replaces it.

**4. Plain Arch and derivatives:**

- Limine: the same drop-in, then `sudo limine-update`
- systemd-boot: append to `options` in `/boot/loader/entries/*.conf`
- GRUB:

```bash
sudo sed -i 's/^GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT="/&amdgpu.dcdebugmask=0x400 /' /etc/default/grub
sudo grub-mkconfig -o /boot/grub/grub.cfg
```

Reboot.

If `0x400` stops the freeze but some flicker remains, move to `0x410`, then `0x610`, one reboot each.
problems.verify:
```bash
cat /sys/module/amdgpu/parameters/dcdebugmask   # 1024 for 0x400, 1040 for 0x410, 1552 for 0x610
cat /proc/cmdline
```

On Omarchy 4, `/proc/cmdline` must still contain Omarchy's defaults (`quiet splash loglevel=0 ... initramfs_async=0`). Then use the desktop normally on a bright page, or log out and back in to the greeter: the panel must keep updating and not flicker.
problems.danger:
Disabling Panel Replay and PSR costs idle battery on the internal panel, because the GPU has to scan out every frame. The parameter itself cannot break boot.

The drop-in is the real risk. A bare `=` instead of `+=`, or a file name that sorts before `omarchy-defaults.conf`, discards Omarchy's defaults including `initramfs_async=0`, which can leave an encrypted machine at an unthemed text LUKS prompt. `limine-mkinitcpio` rewrites the UKI on the ESP, so check `df -h /boot` first. A full ESP produces a truncated image. Do not enable Omarchy Direct Boot while you are still testing parameters, because it bypasses the Limine menu you would recover from.

problems.title: Fix blank or black GTK4 windows (Nautilus, Loupe) on NVIDIA with a second GPU
problems.symptom:
